@@31716818 <h> In the Age of the Coronavirus , Biden 's ' Results ' Require Bernie 's ' Revolution ' <p> Every bar and restaurant in Ohio , California , Illinois , and Massachusetts will be closed on Monday and for a long time thereafter . The nation 's largest school districts have shuttered their classrooms . Virtually all major conferences , sporting events , and concerts in the United States have been canceled . And in its latest advisory , the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention implored Americans not to convene or attend any gatherings of more than 50 people for ( at least ) the next eight weeks . <p> Much of Europe and Asia is no longer open for business either . In their ( necessary ) efforts to prevent the novel coronavirus from overwhelming hospital systems the world over , policymakers have engineered a global recession the likes of which no one has ever seen . @@31730119 <h> The right dose of geoengineering could reduce climate change risks , study says <p> Stratospheric aerosol geoengineering is the idea that adding a layer of aerosol particles to the upper atmosphere can reduce climate changes caused by greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide . <p> Previous research shows that solar geoengineering could be achieved using commercially available aircraft technologies to deliver the particles at a cost of a few billion dollars per year and would reduce global average temperatures . However , the question remains whether this approach could reduce important climate hazards at a regional level . That is , could it reduce region-by-region changes in water availability or extreme temperatures ? <p> Results from a new study by UCL and Harvard researchers suggest that even a crude method like injecting sulphur dioxide in the stratosphere could reduce many important climate hazards without making any region obviously worse off . <p> The findings , published today in Environmental Research Letters , used results from a sophisticated simulation of stratospheric aerosol geoengineering to evaluate whether the approach could offset or worsen the effects of climate change around the world . How these effects differed under different temperature scenarios @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ warming by adding aerosols to the stratosphere could moderate important climate hazards in almost all regions . They saw an exacerbation of the effects of climate change in only a very small fraction of land areas . <p> Lead author , Professor Peter Irvine ( UCL Earth Sciences ) , said : " Most studies focus on a scenario where solar geoengineering offsets all future warming . While this reduces overall climate change substantially , we show that in these simulations , it goes too far in some respects leading to about 9% of the land area experiencing greater climate change , i.e. seeing the effects of climate change exacerbated . <p> " However , if instead only half the warming is offset , then we find that stratospheric aerosol geoengineering could still reduce climate change overall but would only exacerbate change over 1.3% of the land area . " <p> The team emphasise that solar geoengineering only treats the symptoms of climate change and not the underlying cause , which is the build-up of CO2 and other greenhouse gases in the atmosphere . It should therefore be considered as @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ address climate change . <p> The study is a follow-up to a paper published last year in Nature Climate Change showed similar results when solar geoengineering was approximated by simply turning down the sun . That prior study begged the question : would the results hold up with a more realistic simulation using injection of sulphur dioxide , the simplest known method of solar geoengineering . <p> " Our results suggest that when used at the right dose and alongside reductions in greenhouse gas emissions , stratospheric aerosol geoengineering could be useful for managing the impacts of climate change . However , there are still many uncertainties about the potential effects of stratospheric aerosol geoengineering and more research is needed to know if this idea is truly viable , " added Dr. Irvine . <p> The team used data from the Geoengineering Large Ensemble Study , which used a sophisticated climate-chemistry model to simulate the climate response to a hypothetical deployment of stratospheric aerosol geoengineering . In this model study , sulphur dioxide was released at different latitudes in the Tropics to produce a layer of aerosols tuned to keep @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ The researchers focused on changes in mean and extreme temperature , changes in water availability and changes in extreme precipitation , i.e. climate variables that determine key climate risks . <p> Previous work suggested that stratospheric aerosol geoengineering could lead to a substantial weakening of monsoons and an intensification of drought . However , the authors found that in those regions where halving warming with stratospheric aerosol geoengineering exacerbated change , it increased water availability rather than reduced it . This suggests that concerns that stratospheric aerosol geoengineering could lead to aridification and drought could be misplaced . <p> Co-author , Professor David Keith ( Harvard 's Engineering and Applied Sciences and Kennedy school ) , said : " Early research with climate models consistently shows that spatially uniform solar radiation modification could significantly reduce climate risks when combined with emissions cuts . But , should we trust the models ? Uncertainties are deep and no single result is trustworthy , but this paper is a step towards more realistic modelling from injection to regional impacts . " <p> The team are now researching the projected effects of stratospheric aerosolgeoengineering @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ understand the potential benefits and risks to society and ecosystems . <p> Citation : The right dose of geoengineering could reduce climate change risks , study says ( 2020 , March 19 ) retrieved 21 March 2020 from https : **39;5652;TOOLONG ... @@31738322 <p> It was another bad year on the Colorado River , and the numbers prove it . <p> River flows into Lake Powell at the Arizona-Utah border were 43 percent of normal in water year 2017-2018 , which ended at the end of last month . That 's the lowest since the extreme drought year of 2002 , when they were 24 percent of normal . It 's the third lowest annual flow into Powell since records on river flows started being kept in 1906 . <p> The river 's annual flows were above average in only four of the 19 years since 2000 . This was the river 's driest 19-year period on record . <p> The combined storage of river water in Lake Powell and Lake Mead is about 41 percent of normal . It 's the lowest combined storage since Lake Powell was filling during the mid-1960s after the closing of the gates at the newly constructed Glen Canyon Dam . <p> This year 's flows into Lake Powell were far less than the federal forecast back in April of about 52 percent of normal . One reason is that flows into Powell were 1 percent @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ and 2 percent of normal in August -- the second driest on record . <p> " We had a pretty good year in 2017 , with an inflow into Powell of 110 percent of average . But unfortunately we lost that storage and a little bit more in 2018 , " said Dan Bunk , a U.S. Bureau of Reclamation hydrologist . <p> He presented these and other figures Wednesday at a meeting of the steering committee working on a proposed Drought Contingency Plan for the river 's Lower Basin . <p> " Really that buffer that we saw in Lake Powell , the extra storage that helped protect the Colorado River system , was lost this year , " Bunk said . <p> The bureau predicts a 57 percent chance of the river 's first shortage in 2020 , with the odds of shortages increasing in future years . That would happen if Lake Mead drops below 1,075 feet at the end of 2019 . <p> Without a formal Drought Contingency Plan in place , under which less water would be used , there 's about a 75 percent @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ which would require deeper cuts in deliveries , the bureau says . <p> That 's based on assuming the trends of declining river flows from 1988 to 2015 continues . With a drought plan , the odds of Mead dropping below 1,050 by then fall to a little over 50 percent . <p> Without a drought plan , there 's also at least a 40 percent chance of Mead dropping below 1,025 feet from 2024 through 2026 , bureau figures show , based on the same 1988-2015 flow record . With a plan , the odds of such low levels drops to less than 20 percent for all those years and to as low as 10 percent in 2024 . <p> At 1,025 feet , a federal takeover of how the river 's flows are divided is possible , as federal officials would want to keep the lake from sinking lower and approaching " dead pool " at 895 feet , when no water could be pulled from Mead . <h> Get local news delivered to your inbox ! <p> Tony graduated from Northwestern University and started at the Star @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ 2005 , focusing on water supplies , climate change , the Rosemont Mine and the endangered jaguar . <p> A drought contingency plan , which still requires approval by lawmakers and others , would pay to have water previously stored underground pumped out to be used to meet at least some the needs of farmers and others who otherwise would find themselves going without .

Until then , I think visits to the very laudable and much more affordable Ikanos would do very well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Peter Hum ate at Ikanos as a guest of Montreal En Lumiere. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;18959;TOOLONG " **32;18986;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumFri , 28 Feb 2020 17:00:24 **45;19020;TOOLONG ... of Ottawa 's modern franchise : What 's behind Ottawa 's changing food scenehttp : **35;19067;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;19104;TOOLONG ... title= " Pi Co is a new pizza franchise that has spread from Toronto to Ottawa . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;19140;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1562659 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;19170;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the beginning of this year , quietly but clearly , franchise fever climbed up a notch in Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Westboro , workers at the brand new Pi Co. stretched dough balls to make Neapolitan pizzas , then slid pies with their customer-chosen toppings into a sleek white ceramic pizza oven for a 90-second spin in 715 F heat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I decided to venture into something new . I wanted to make people happy on the spot , &amp;rdquo ; says Pi Co. &amp;rsquo ; s owner-operator Chris McCrudden , explaining his switch from working in retail to opening a restaurant . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 37-year-old already plans to open a second location downtown , at Metcalfe and Nepean streets , this spring , and has larger dreams of expanding into the suburbs . &amp;ldquo ; The plan is to scale across the city , &amp;rdquo ; McCrudden says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He adds : &amp;ldquo ; Everyone likes pizza and nobody&amp;rsquo ; s doing this . You can&amp;rsquo ; t find pizza like this anywhere . &amp;rdquo ; That is , except in Toronto , where Pi Co. has opened 16 locations since 2016. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19206;TOOLONG ... title= " Pi Co is a new pizza franchise that has spread from Toronto to Ottawa . Chris McCrudden opened his first location in late January and plans to open a second one downtown this spring . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;19242;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1563197 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , in the ByWard Market , staff at the just-opened Dal Moro&amp;rsquo ; s Fresh Pasta To Go were doling out spanking fresh , made-in-house rigatoni , spaghetti , fusilli and linguine swaddled in pools of sauce in their take-out cartons , following the processes and recipes chef Gabriele Dal Moro instituted at his tiny store in Venice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t find something like that in North America , &amp;rdquo ; says Santhosh Reddy , the Toronto-based master franchisor for Dal Moro&amp;rsquo ; s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Reddy asserts that while you can get fresh pasta at some restaurants and quick-service pasta at many others , Dal Moro&amp;rsquo ; s is the only business that unites fresh pasta and quick service . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a unique model . There&amp;rsquo ; s nobody who&amp;rsquo ; s doing it right now , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Reddy visited Venice in late 2016 to celebrate his wedding anniversary and liked chef Dal Moro&amp;rsquo ; s business and food there so much that he resolved to bring the concept to Canada . By the spring of 2018 , Reddy had opened the first of his four Dal Moro&amp;rsquo ; s in Toronto . He says he envisions opening two more Ottawa locations in the next two years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa has no shortage of pizza and pasta eateries , either independently operated or run as a corporate chain location or franchise . But Pi Co. and Dal Moro&amp;rsquo ; s , which are the inaugural Ottawa locations of relatively new Toronto-based companies , are part of a larger wave of recently arrived franchises of companies that are headquartered elsewhere in Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19272;TOOLONG ... title= " Mohammad Shaik makes a fresh batch of spaghetti to be served in dishes of Dal Moro 's fresh pasta to go , apparently a unique concept that serves fresh pasta in a quick service model . " alt= " Mohammad Shaik makes a fresh batch of spaghetti to be served in dishes of Dal Moro 's fresh pasta to go , apparently a unique concept that serves fresh pasta in a quick service model . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;19308;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1563223 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the last four or five years , restaurant industry watchers say , franchise restaurants , both next-generation and old-guard , have expanded their presence in Canada , especially in urban centres , in sync with changing demographics and dining-out preferences . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Millennials with specific preferences when they go out to eat &amp;mdash ; think predilections for convenience , speedy service , vegan and vegetarian options , organic ingredients , sustainable eating &amp;mdash ; are creating demand for new kinds of franchises that feel very 2020 . ( Among the earliest franchise locations to open in Canada were A&amp;amp ; W in 1956 , McDonald&amp;rsquo ; s in 1967 and the Canadian company Pizza Pizza in the late 1960s. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Demand , too , is fuelled by the cultural diversification of urban centres . The multicultural breadth of restaurants may be most striking in Vancouver or Toronto , but Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s dining-out scene is arguably responding to a change in the population makeup . Why else , for example , would the Taiwanese bubble tea franchises Presotea , Chatime and CoCo come to town in recent years , or , for that matter , the Montreal-based globally minded sandwich franchise Centrale Bergham ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here&amp;rsquo ; s another sign of the shift in restaurant franchises : It would have been laughable , years ago , for this newspaper&amp;rsquo ; s restaurant critic to review an East Side Mario&amp;rsquo ; s , or for that matter , a Milestones . But in the last few years , I&amp;rsquo ; ve reviewed franchises including Sansotei , the Centretown ramen mainstay , and Yunshang Rice Noodle , a few blocks south on Bank Street , where Chinese &amp;ldquo ; Crossing the Bridge&amp;rdquo ; noodles are the delicious specialty . I&amp;rsquo ; d be missing out if I didn&amp;rsquo ; t pay attention to these franchises , as their respective soups are arguably the best of their kind in town . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There is a huge paradigm shift in the food service industry , &amp;rdquo ; says Altaf Sovani , academic chair of Algonquin College&amp;rsquo ; s school of hospitality and tourism . &amp;ldquo ; You have brand new , creative innovative chains coming , quick-service franchises or fast casual , they are going all over Canada now . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19338;TOOLONG ... title= " Coconut curry broth at Yunshang Rice Noodle. " alt= " Coconut curry broth at Yunshang Rice Noodle. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;19374;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1563201 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Asad Amin , vice-president of Ipsos Food and Beverage group , says that as recently as four years ago , independent restaurants were outpacing chain restaurants nationally . But since then , Amin says he&amp;rsquo ; s seen stronger growth among chains outpacing independents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Independents are growing still nationally , but chains and franchises are overtaking them , &amp;rdquo ; Amin says . In particular , premium casual and upscale fast-casual restaurants are on the rise nationally , he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dal Moro&amp;rsquo ; s Reddy , who was a business analyst before he jumped into the restaurant business , says Ottawa is ripe for not just his business but other new franchises as well . &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s more demand for new types of food . We wanted to be part of the changing scene . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That scene will include several Toronto-based franchises not far from Reddy&amp;rsquo ; s pasta business . Gyubee , an all-you-can-eat Japanese barbecue restaurant , opened early February at York and Dalhousie streets . Further south on Dalhousie , a franchise of the Taiwanese business Hot-Star , which specializes in crispy and massive chicken cutlets , is to open , continuing its expansion beyond Asia in North America . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Further afield , by this summer , the hip Toronto-based chain The Burger&amp;rsquo ; s Priest , which has more than 20 locations in the Greater Toronto Area , expects to have two locations open in Ottawa , one on Baseline Road near Clyde Avenue and then another on Bank Street near Heron Road . Elgin Street awaits a franchise of the international sandwich maker German D&amp;ouml ; ner Kebab , a few doors down from locations of the Japanese cheesecake chain Uncle Tetsu and The Fry , a franchise that sells Korean fried chicken . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The newcomers will join recent arrivals to Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s franchise landscape such as the Chocolats Favoris shops in Kanata , Barrhaven , Orl&amp;eacute ; ans and Gatineau , the over-the-top burger place La Belle et La Boeuf in Gatineau , rotisserie chicken place Benny &amp;amp ; Co. in Orl&amp;eacute ; ans and the Centrale Bergham sandwich shops . All of these businesses expanded from Quebec into the Ottawa-Gatineau area . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alex Rechichi , CEO of the Crave It Restaurant Group in Oakville , calls The Burger&amp;rsquo ; s Priest , a chain in his group&amp;rsquo ; s portfolio , &amp;ldquo ; the anti-corporate corporate brand , &amp;rdquo ; because its practices , such as using &amp;ldquo ; ultra , ultra fresh&amp;rdquo ; meat ground from whole muscle rather than lesser cuts , are rooted in the award-winning and tiny original Burger&amp;rsquo ; s Priest that opened in Toronto in 2010. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We do things like an independent would , &amp;rdquo ; Rechichi says , adding that it was &amp;ldquo ; a natural progression&amp;rdquo ; for The Burger&amp;rsquo ; s Priest to come to Ottawa given the past successes that some of Rechichi&amp;rsquo ; s previous ventures , including Mucho Burrito and Extreme Pita , enjoyed here . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19404;TOOLONG ... title= " A burger from The Burger 's Priest . ( Credit : The Burger 's Priest ) " alt= " A burger from The Burger 's Priest . ( Credit : The Burger 's Priest ) " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;19440;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1563216 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , for all of their attributes , franchises still have their skeptics and detractors. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Not surprisingly , Stephen Beckta , one of Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s leadings restaurateurs whose businesses include Beckta Dining &amp;amp ; Wine , Play Food &amp;amp ; Wine and Gezellig , prefers to support independent restaurants . &amp;ldquo ; On the whole , there is usually much more soul to them than chains that are designed and run from afar , &amp;rdquo ; Beckta says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Beckta says he doesn&amp;rsquo ; t avoid chain restaurants outright , and he even lauds The Works , which got its start in Ottawa before expanding widely across Ontario , because his son is a big fan of its burgers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But he continues : &amp;ldquo ; There are some things they ( chains and franchises ) do very well , and we independents can always learn from ( them ) , &amp;rdquo ; Beckta continues . &amp;ldquo ; But my default is always to support , and enjoy , the small chef- and owner-operated spots in Ottawa . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Similarly , Chris Knight , CEO of the Ottawa-based food-show production company Gusto Worldwide Media , places much higher value on independent restaurants over franchises and chains . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For starters , Knight points out that last month at the Canadian Culinary Championships in Ottawa , where a dozen Canadian chefs representing their respective regions vied for the champion&amp;rsquo ; s prize , none of the chef-testants came from franchise or chain operations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The innovation and creativity still remains in the smaller restaurant , typically ones where the chef still works the line and smells like onions and garlic , &amp;rdquo ; says Knight . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And while franchise operators are proud to consistently serve the same food from location to location , building up the trust of customers who want a familiar , reliable experience , Knight decries the homogeneity of dining scenes that can arise . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Small companies are the ones that innovate , &amp;rdquo ; Knight contends . &amp;ldquo ; Large companies are the ones that have plastic-coated menus where the food is the same everywhere . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Knight&amp;rsquo ; s view , Lansdowne Park&amp;rsquo ; s franchise-heavy array of restaurants &amp;mdash ; from Jack Astor&amp;rsquo ; s Bar and Grill to Milestones to the pizza place Industria Pizzeria to Joey Lansdowne &amp;mdash ; is a collection of formulaic , too-similar businesses that eat into the revenues of independent restaurants not just in the neighbouring Glebe but the city at large . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s sad indeed with smaller restaurants fighting to survive , &amp;rdquo ; Knight says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19470;TOOLONG ... title= " Streetscapes 's of franchised restaurants in Lansdowne , Sunday , February 9 , 2020. " alt= " Streetscapes 's of franchised restaurants in Lansdowne , Sunday , February 9 , 2020. " data-portal-copyright= " Ashley Fraser " **28;19506;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1563220 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; That feeling of d&amp;eacute ; j&amp;agrave ; vu ( or deja mang&amp;eacute ; ) can rear its head when you realize that when it comes to many chains and franchises , especially in shopping mall food courts , big-box mall parking lots and highway-side rest stops , they are properties of a handful of massive restaurant companies that aggregate a multitude of brands in their portfolios . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For example , Toronto-based Recipe Unlimited Co. ( formerly Cara Operations Ltd. ) tallied 208 corporate chain locations and more than 1,100 franchise locations in its Sept. 29 , 2019 management&amp;rsquo ; s discussion and analyst statement , including locations of Swiss Chalet , Harvey&amp;rsquo ; s , Montana&amp;rsquo ; s , East Side Mario&amp;rsquo ; s , Milestones and The Keg. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Montreal-based Foodtastic has such brands as La Belle et La Boeuf , the pizzeria Monza , the sushi eatery Blossom and Big Rig Kitchen and Brewery . Last summer , Foodtastic bought a majority stake in that Ottawa-based business , launched in 2012 by former Ottawa Senators defenceman Chris &amp;ldquo ; Big Rig&amp;rdquo ; Phillips . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among Canadian franchise aggregators , the Montreal-based MTY Food Group may have the largest number of brands under its banner &amp;mdash ; almost 80 of them , ranging from Thai Express and Extreme Pita to The Works to Mucho Burrito to the steak-centric restaurants Houston and Madisons. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Ottawa , the concentration of franchises is most clearly seen in its suburbs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of Barrhaven&amp;rsquo ; s 90 restaurants , about half of them are franchises , a third of them are owner-operated , and the rest are chains , says Andrea Steenbakkers , executive director of the Barrhaven BIA. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She explains that Barrhaven , located beyond the Greenbelt and bounded by Highway 416 and the Rideau River , is its &amp;ldquo ; own little entity , &amp;rdquo ; a community of 100,000 that is less &amp;ldquo ; **30;19536;TOOLONG ; than downtown Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Not a lot of people are coming to Barrhaven for restaurants , &amp;rdquo ; she says . Restaurant-goers are largely residents of the suburb , and indeed , so too are most of the franchise owners , says Steenbakkers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; These ( franchise ) restaurants are really firmly rooted in our community , &amp;rdquo ; she says , adding that the profits of these businesses ultimately circulate within the suburb&amp;rsquo ; s economy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She sees the appeal of franchises for their operators . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a simple way for people to go into business , &amp;rdquo ; she says , with a business model , training and other aspects already well-developed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That said , Steenbakkers says she would like to see more owner-operated restaurants in Barrhaven , and she names the veteran pasta place La Porto A Casa , the Chinese eatery Golden Restaurant and newcomer Italian restaurant Juluca&amp;rsquo ; s as notable independent successes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Kanata North BIA , which covers March Road and the western stretch of Carling Avenue , counted 17 franchises among its list of 37 restaurants , including a Big Rig , two Subways and three Tim Hortons locations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Kanata Central BIA , which includes the Kanata Centrum and Signature Centre shopping centres , says that 16 of its 30 member restaurants are franchises. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , at Kanata Centrum , there are signs of franchise renewal . While familiar high-volume restaurants Milestones , Jack Astor&amp;rsquo ; s , Baton Rouge and Boston Pizza take up the largest lots , tucked away is the wee franchise Bangkok Buri , which exemplifies some smaller-scale but contemporary thinking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19568;TOOLONG ... title= " Mikhael Absi , manager of Bangkok Buri with a plate of penang curry , in front of one of his colourful evocative walls . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;19604;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1563195 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are just two Bangkok Buris &amp;mdash ; &amp;nbsp ; one at Union Station in Toronto and the Kanata location , which opened in September 2018 . ( The franchise&amp;rsquo ; s website says a Barrhaven location is in the offing. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Kanata , its operator is Mikhael Absi , a veteran of Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s franchise scene who in the last 27 years has been involved in a Quiznos , an East Side Mario&amp;rsquo ; s and a Baton Rouge , to give a partial list . Absi also opened five Mucho Burritos in Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Absi is Lebanese , not Thai , and he first cooked Thai food in 2018 . But he says Bangkok Buri&amp;rsquo ; s food has its own virtues , including ingredients cut freshly every day &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; nothing is pre-made , &amp;rdquo ; he says &amp;mdash ; and many vegan and gluten-free options . &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s a biggie , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bangkok Buri&amp;rsquo ; s fast-casual fare also has some foodie cred because the dishes that Absi executes were developed in collaboration with Toronto restaurateur Monte Wan , who owns the well-regarded Thai restaurants Khao San Road and Nana . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Absi&amp;rsquo ; s a staunch advocate for franchises because if they&amp;rsquo ; re good , they engender trust among their customers . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a matter of knowing who to go back to , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ipsos vice-president Amin says the increasing culinary diversity of franchises and chains such as Bangkok Buri speaks to the cross-acculturation of the dining public , which would include both expats from countries whose food is being served and &amp;ldquo ; young local Canadians , well travelled and with diverse palates&amp;rdquo ; seeking dishes they have eaten abroad or are curious to try . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Amin adds that when he looks at the uptake of dishes from other cultures , for example from Asian countries , consumption by Asian expatriates is actually declining , while demand is growing among other Canadians . The bottom line is that the changing tastes of the larger public is fuelling the success of these &amp;ldquo ; multicultural&amp;rdquo ; restaurants , Amin says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; About 100 metres away from Bangkok Buri is the first of Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s Mary Brown&amp;rsquo ; s Chicken &amp;amp ; Taters franchises. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19634;TOOLONG ... title= " The staff of Mary Brown 's Chicken and Taters pose for a photo with chicken . From left : Muskan Sandhu , Sukheep Kaur , Jane Arenburg , and Sam Paquette. " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;19670;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1563196 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rooted in the original Mary Brown&amp;rsquo ; s fried chicken eatery that opened in St. John&amp;rsquo ; s , Newfoundland five decades ago , the Kanata Mary Brown&amp;rsquo ; s opened in early 2019 . Some fried chicken lovers would say its arrival is long overdue &amp;mdash ; &amp;nbsp ; it is one of more than 150 Mary Brown&amp;rsquo ; s locations across Canada . Mary Brown&amp;rsquo ; s locations have since opened on Carling Avenue in the Cineplex Ottawa parking lot and in Barrhaven , at the Chapman Mills Marketplace retail district . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Like many of the recently arrived franchises , Mary Brown&amp;rsquo ; s stresses freshness and on-site preparation . Sahal Sidana , its manager , adds that the chicken he serves is also halal &amp;mdash ; butchered in keeping with Islamic strictures so that Muslim customers can partake. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sidana , a 24-year-old who came to Canada from India , studied culinary management at Algonquin College before he joined the Mary Brown&amp;rsquo ; s team . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He said he had thought of opening a restaurant of his own , but then thought better of it , when he pondered the investment required and the recipes that would have to be developed , among other things . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You&amp;rsquo ; re not sure that people even like it , &amp;rdquo ; he added . Whereas when Mary Brown&amp;rsquo ; s came to Kanata , there was instant buzz , Sidana says , because its crispy , golden-battered reputation preceded it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Opening a franchise is much better than opening your own restaurant , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; You don&amp;rsquo ; t need to do a lot of hard work ( that ) you can easily get through the company . Of course , that&amp;rsquo ; s not a bad thing . However , I&amp;rsquo ; m more keen to dine out when the fare is indulgent or intriguing , in addition to being good for me . I can make my own grain bowls at home , thank you very much . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But if you scroll down the eatery&amp;rsquo ; s home page , the intrigue mounts . There&amp;rsquo ; s a reference in a photo to Bukhari serving &amp;ldquo ; Arabian food . &amp;rdquo ; What would that be ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The only way for me to find out was to step away from the screen and head over to the place . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During my visits to Bukhari , it turned out that its Arabian food was generally as tasty as it was affordable and unpretentious . Also , the kind and friendly staff there were happy to specify that Bukhari served dishes with their roots in Yemen , the country that sits south of Saudi Arabia on the Arabian Peninsula , closer to Africa than it is to , say , Iran . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now , I can affirm that Bukhari serves the best Yemeni food I&amp;rsquo ; ve had , which , it should be said , is also the only Yemeni food I&amp;rsquo ; ve had . Bukhari , which replaced the top-notch casual Middle Eastern restaurant Pita Bell Kabab after its westward move on Carling Avenue , is one of the very few Yemeni restaurants in Ottawa . ( I&amp;rsquo ; ve since learned of House of Mandi on Hunt Club Road as well. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Its food is halal , prepared to Islamic strictures , and lamb and chicken are the featured meats , although a beef dish or two can also be found . The meats can be grilled , fried , steamed or stewed. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some menu items were familiar and less specifically Yemeni , including chicken and beef kebabs , chicken tikka , tabbouleh and Greek salad . But most dishes here were Yemeni &amp;mdash ; lesser known to me and listed with no descriptions . We had to ask about dishes such as chicken mandi and lamb haneed , and we were glad that we did . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Before any of our orders at lunch or dinner arrived , we were given small but appetite-whetting bowls of nicely seasoned lamb broth , served with wedges of lime on the side . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s welcome soup , &amp;rdquo ; one of the female staffers told me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Speaking of appetite-whetting , the only appetizer we tried at Bukhari was its baba ghanouj ( $6 ) , which was fresher , more herbal and much less smoky than other renditions I&amp;rsquo ; ve had of that eggplant dip . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19959;TOOLONG ... title= " Pita and house-made babaghanouj at Bukhari " alt= " Pita and house-made babaghanouj at Bukhari " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;19995;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1558814 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hearty appetites would do well with one of the generous platters that pair a heap of long-grain rice with bone-in lamb or chicken . In chicken bukhari ( $18 ) , the tender half-bird was tucked in a mound of mildly spiced rice with slivers of carrot . Lamb haneed ( $18 ) kept its rice , garnished with fried onions , separate from a foil packet filled with delectable pieces of lamb . Lamb mandi ( $18 ) delivered pieces of shank and rib , both flavourful and toothsome , on top of rice garnished with fried onions and slivers of almonds . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20025;TOOLONG ... title= " Lamb haneed at Bukhari " alt= " Lamb haneed at Bukhari " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20061;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1558909 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20091;TOOLONG ... title= " Lamb mandi , lamb broth , salad , spicy dip at Bukhari " alt= " Lamb mandi , lamb broth , salad , spicy dip at Bukhari " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20127;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1559942 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20157;TOOLONG ... title= " Chicken Mandi from Bukhari restaurant " alt= " Chicken Mandi from Bukhari restaurant " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20193;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1560040 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; All of these dishes came with plates of simply dressed green salad , dusted with tangy sumac , and a spicy , salsa-like condiment also landed on our table . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We didn&amp;rsquo ; t try Bukhari&amp;rsquo ; s biryani rice dishes , which we were told were the spiciest among the menu . The former was accessibly tasty and quick to disappear when scooped up with pita bread . The accompaniment is called holba , and by itself , it was bracingly bitter . If I order fahsa again , I&amp;rsquo ; ll trying blending some of it into the stew for another layer of flavour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20421;TOOLONG ... title= " Fahsa ( lamb stew ) at Bukhari " alt= " Fahsa ( lamb stew ) at Bukhari " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20457;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1560044 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bukhari serves breakfast , too , with a few dishes that are specific to the morning meal and some , such as fried lamb and lamb liver , that are served all day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We ordered shakshouka ( $6 ) , which elsewhere has been a dish of eggs in a spicy tomato sauce , and received instead something closer to a scrambled omelet , which was good and homey just the same . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20487;TOOLONG ... title= " Shakshouka eggs at Bukhari " alt= " Shakshouka eggs at Bukhari " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20523;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1558806 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; We also had foul ( $7 ) , which was a savoury kidney bean dip served with pita . Food ReviewsDining Out : Spectacular dinner at Atelier proves it 's still the best in the gamehttp : **36;20965;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;21003;TOOLONG ... title= " Vegetarian version of the guinea fowl liver mousse served recently at Atelier on Rochester Street " alt= " Vegetarian version of the guinea fowl liver mousse served recently at Atelier on Rochester Street " data-portal-copyright= " Alison Mah " **28;21039;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1554228 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; **36;21069;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; 540 Rochester St. , Ottawa , 613-321-3537 , &lt;a href= " http : //atelierrestaurant.ca " &gt;atelier ... &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Open : &lt;/strong&gt; For dinner Tuesday through Saturday , closed Sunday and Monday &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Prices : &lt;/strong&gt; $125 for a 12-course tasting menu &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Access : &lt;/strong&gt; Steps to front door &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Not to brag , but so far in 2020 , I&amp;rsquo ; ve already had two fantastic , 12-course , haute-cuisine dinners . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last Saturday night at the Shaw Centre , there was the opulent , gourmet&amp;rsquo ; s race-against-the-clock that was the grand finale of the 2020 Canadian Culinary Championships . Completist that I am , I hit every station and ate beautiful plate after beautiful plate , savouring delicacy-rich creations from some of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s leading chefs. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And then there was my other fine-dining meal , which was even better . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In mid-January , I had the blind , 12-course menu at Atelier . And as vaunted as the culinary championships&amp;rsquo ; delights were , dinner at chef-owner Marc Lepine&amp;rsquo ; s cutting-edge restaurant on Rochester Street topped them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Perhaps that&amp;rsquo ; s not so surprising . Atelier has been consistently lauded since it opened in late 2008 , landing on various renowned lists of elite restaurants in Canada and North America . Lepine took home the gold at the 2012 and 2016 Canadian Culinary Championships , which were held in Kelowna , B.C. , before the event moved to Ottawa this year . Canada&amp;rsquo ; s principal assessor of restaurants and chefs , the annual Canada&amp;rsquo ; s 100 Best Restaurants magazine , named Lepine the country&amp;rsquo ; s most innovative chef in 2018. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I last had dinner at Atelier in 2011 , when four of us marked some birthdays there . It was an evening of wows and irreproachable service , although these are the recollections of a &amp;ldquo ; civilian&amp;rdquo ; diner and not a pro critic &amp;mdash ; I didn&amp;rsquo ; t start this reviewing gig until 2012. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So in 2020 , I was curious to appraise Atelier from my critic&amp;rsquo ; s vantage point , in light of the culinary championships and taking into account developments in Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s restaurant scene in recent years . Not the least of those was the opening last May of THRU , Lepine&amp;rsquo ; s hyper-exclusive six-seat restaurant ( or second-storey private dining room under Atelier&amp;rsquo ; s roof , if you prefer ) that serves an entirely different and mind-boggling menu , all the while relying on Atelier&amp;rsquo ; s kitchen and staff . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After more than a decade , the specific restaurant experience Atelier and Lepine offer should be well-known to discerning food lovers in Ottawa and elsewhere . ( Lepine even published his lavish and revelatory Atelier : The Cookbook in 2018 , which he wrote with my predecessor , Anne DesBrisay. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;21107;TOOLONG ... title= " Renowned local chef Marc Lepine has just released a new cookbook , entitled " Atelier , " after his downtown restaurant . " alt= " Renowned local chef Marc Lepine has just released a new cookbook , entitled " Atelier , " after his downtown restaurant . " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;21143;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1267969 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; DesBrisay herself reviewed Atelier in early 2009 , and her glowing take can be distilled to two short sentences : &amp;ldquo ; This is a brilliantly creative place . Tweak the budget &lt;span class= " marktxzffl3oz " &gt;and&lt;/span&gt; book a table . &amp;rdquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ll note that then , the tasting menu cost $75 , not the $125 of 2020 . I&amp;rsquo ; ll also note , to put that price further in context , that eating at Atelier is in fact a bargain compared to the cost of dining at some not dissimilar Michelin-starred restaurants in the U.S. and abroad . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To achieve his brilliance , Lepine has become a national master of what used to be called molecular gastronomy but is now more usually called modernist cuisine , building on the technological and even chemistry-based innovations of such landmark restaurants as El Bulli in Spain and Alinea in Chicago , where Lepine did an unpaid internship. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One feature of modernist cuisine is the transformation of ingredients into chips , powders , gels and more , maximizing the surprises and the assorted visual and flavour-based balancing acts on the plate . Some dismiss modernist cuisine as pretentious and overly artificial , but I&amp;rsquo ; m OK with it , and prefer to view dinner at Atelier as a parade of highly technical dishes that strive for uniqueness in multiple ways while appealing to a guest&amp;rsquo ; s senses of curiosity and playfulness . Another way of looking at Atelier is that it&amp;rsquo ; s simply Lepine&amp;rsquo ; s forum for showing off what he can do with food . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is a bit of a disconnect between the feel of Atelier and the ambience that some would associate with luxurious , expensive dining . Atelier has always been more minimalist and funky rather than posh and oversized , surrounding guests in the cosy , narrow quarters of a former Little Italy house , amid a stark but not uncomfortable atmosphere of grey , black and white . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Perhaps the goal is to have the creativity of Lepine&amp;rsquo ; s food pop more against such neutrality . For a fine-dining experience , Atelier can even seem on the casual side &amp;mdash ; or at least , in January , I saw guests dressed as casually for their groundbreaking dinner as they would have been at a fast-food outlet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Appearances aside , Atelier indisputably operates at a fine-dining level when it comes to service . The tone set by our servers was unfailingly attentive but never intrusive . Lepine serves the kind of novel , at times arcane fare that requires 30-second-long recitations of ingredients and techniques , and our servers were up to those challenges . The flawlessness of service included that extra-mile measure of re-folding a guest&amp;rsquo ; s crumpled napkin when the guest had left the table . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My predecessor&amp;rsquo ; s 2009 review managed the feat of sharing very , very little about what she ate as she didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to give away too many surprises . I will offer some specifics , based on the fact that my friend and I tried not only the night&amp;rsquo ; s tasting menu but also the vegetarian/vegan alternatives . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Our dinner began very strongly with a snack course that put three mind-expanding bites on a whimsically rotating platform . Who , apart from Lepine , knew that snail caviar , parsnip pur&amp;eacute ; e and crisp , cedar-tinged puff would be delicious ? So , too , was a seaweed crisp topped with crab salad . Just as great was a cube of wagyu beef short rib in sticky soy caramel . We had vegan options , too , which swapped frozen coconut pearls for snail caviar , artichoke salad for crab salad and sweet potato for beef . They were fine , but the carnivore options struck us as the real deal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;21173;TOOLONG ... title= " ( Vegan ) snacks at Atelier " alt= " ( Vegan ) snacks at Atelier " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;21209;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1554296 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A mushroom tom yum dish , garnishing exotic mushrooms with smoked apple dust and more , was fantastic . The vegan version , which left out fish sauce , was just a little less complex and great . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;21239;TOOLONG ... title= " Atelier 's mushroom tom yum course " alt= " Atelier 's mushroom tom yum course " data-portal-copyright= " Alison Mah " **28;21275;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1554299 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among other courses , some were very good but short of a wow , especially in this meat-eater&amp;rsquo ; s opinion . But there were highlights enough to make me think the meal was worthwhile , including an elaborate dish finished with perfect cauliflower soup , a scallop croquettes dish , a sablefish course , a quail course , and a strikingly garnished beef tenderloin-and-kimchi course . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Guests are told to allot three hours for dinner at Atelier . We were there for a good extra hour and a half , but the food gave us much to talk about . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We didn&amp;rsquo ; t dig into Atelier&amp;rsquo ; s well-regarded wine list , but we heard the restaurant&amp;rsquo ; s sommelier dispensing good information and we each enjoyed a top-notch cocktail , one boozy and the other alcohol-free. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;22097;TOOLONG ... title= " Atelier 's yuzu popsicle green tea drink " alt= " Atelier 's yuzu popsicle green tea drink " data-portal-copyright= " Alison Mah " **28;22133;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1554232 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Having been ahead of the curve for so long , Atelier has seen rivals , more so on the national and international dining scenes , make their own modernist inroads . Out : There 's celebrity-chef sizzle at Grill 41 , but also disappointing , overpriced foodhttp : **36;22924;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;22962;TOOLONG ... title= " Scallops with Granny Smith apple emulsion at Grill 41 in the Lord Elgin Hotel " alt= " Scallops with Granny Smith apple emulsion at Grill 41 in the Lord Elgin Hotel " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;22998;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1549850 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Grill 41&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; 100 Elgin St. ( in the Lord Elgin Hotel ) , 613-569-2126 , &lt;a href= " http : //grill41.ca " &gt;grill41.ca&lt;/a &; ... &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Open : &lt;/strong&gt; daily from 6:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Prices : &lt;/strong&gt; mains at dinner from $22 to $69 &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Access : &lt;/strong&gt; fully accessible &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; The veteran Ottawa chef Ren&amp;eacute ; Rodriguez doesn&amp;rsquo ; t need me to sing his praises , but here goes anyway . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Back in the fall of 2012 , when I was just getting settled into this reviewing gig , a dinner at Rodriguez&amp;rsquo ; s restaurant Navarra blew my mind . The Murray Street business served vibrant , elevated dishes energized by the culinary inspirations of Mexico , which is where Rodriguez&amp;rsquo ; s family is from . After Navarra closed in 2017 , Rodriguez later ran the kitchen at the upscale Italian restaurant Orto in the Glebe . There , we also found the food impressive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even if you haven&amp;rsquo ; t eaten Rodriguez&amp;rsquo ; s best efforts , you may well have rooted for him during his much-publicized TV cooking escapades . He won Top Chef Canada in 2014 . On the 2017 Food Network show Beat Bobby Flay , Rodriguez did just that , prevailing over the American mega-chef. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , this week&amp;rsquo ; s disheartening mystery is why the dishes we&amp;rsquo ; ve had at the Lord Elgin Hotel&amp;rsquo ; s Grill 41 , where Rodriguez has been the chef since last fall , have ranged from alright to so-so to disappointing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since at least mid-November , Rodriguez has held that position at the venerable downtown hotel , reporting to the Lord Elgin&amp;rsquo ; s executive chef Neil Mather , while the restaurant itself is owned and operated by food services giant Sodexo Canada . The revamped menu now includes a slew of &amp;ldquo ; Ren&amp;eacute ; Rodriguez signature dishes , &amp;rdquo ; designated with &amp;ldquo ; RR&amp;rdquo ; beside them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And yet , during my two lunch visits and one dinner , we too often found those dishes and others were scarcely items of which&amp;nbsp ; an accomplished , famous chef should be proud . Some were too casually made , such as an appetizer of dry , overcooked octopus , or too casually conceived , like the entry-level beet salad awash in fris&amp;eacute ; e . The high prices of dishes compounded our disatisfactions. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rodriguez told me this week of the hours he works at Lord Elgin , which are from 3 p.m. to 9 p.m. , five days a week . ( He also works at Mercadito , the taco-based business in the Queen St. Fare food hall . ) He was not in the kitchen when we had dinner . Nor was he hands-on with our lunches . But how much should that matter ? I know that the dinner at Navarra that wowed me years ago was prepared while Rodriguez was absent from his kitchen , by talented cooks who could assemble Rodriguez&amp;rsquo ; s dazzling creations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23028;TOOLONG ... title= " Complimentary cornbread with shisha butter at Grill 41 in the Lord Elgin Hotel " alt= " Complimentary cornbread with shisha butter at Grill 41 in the Lord Elgin Hotel " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;23064;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1549957 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23094;TOOLONG ... title= " Some more disheveled cornbread and shisha butter at another visit to Grill 41 " alt= " Some more disheveled cornbread and shisha butter at another visit to Grill 41 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;23130;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1549967 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; At Grill 41 , we ate best when we had less ambitious fare at our two lunches . Thanks to the heavy-on-the-umami quality of the &amp;ldquo ; RR&amp;rdquo ; truffle burger ( eight ounces of ground chuck , bolstered by truffled triple cream brie and mushroom jam ) , its $25 splurge was palatable , even if its fries were mediocre . The &amp;ldquo ; RR&amp;rdquo ; watercress salad , which matched the greens with cured tuna gravlax , deviled egg and olive powder ( $21 ) was a simple dish , but all of its components were satisfyingly in place . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23160;TOOLONG ... title= " Truffle burger at Grill 41 , with salad and fries " alt= " Truffle burger at Grill 41 , with salad and fries " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;23196;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1549892 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23226;TOOLONG ... title= " Watercress salad with tuna gravlax ( half serving ) at Grill 41 " alt= " Watercress salad with tuna gravlax ( half serving ) at Grill 41 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;23262;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1549854 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; At lunch , we also tried the oddly designated &amp;ldquo ; RR&amp;rdquo ; Wolfgang Puck pizza ( $24 ) , made with Alfredo sauce , shiitake mushroom , arugula , radicchio and truffle , which was reasonably tasty , but also too crisply cooked . For a non-&amp;ldquo ; RR&amp;rdquo ; dish , we went for the highly recommended &amp;ldquo ; Michael Smith&amp;rdquo ; chowder , which must owe its name to the fact that the P.E.I.-based star chef helped develop Grill 41&amp;rsquo ; s menu in 2011 . While the thickly creamy seafood chowder was expensive ( $19 ) and looked as if it had been doled out haphazardly , at least it was generously stocked with shrimp , lobster and other ingredients that were almost surprisingly toothsome and fresh . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23292;TOOLONG ... title= " Wolfgang Puck pizza ( half-serving ) at Grill 41 " alt= " Wolfgang Puck pizza ( half-serving ) at Grill 41 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;23328;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1549895 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23358;TOOLONG ... title= " Michael Smith Chowder at Grill 41 in the Lord Elgin Hotel " alt= " Michael Smith Chowder at Grill 41 in the Lord Elgin Hotel " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;23394;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1549660 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Our dinner at Grill 41 , though , was more uneven and included some &amp;ldquo ; RR&amp;rdquo ; dishes that flopped . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of four appetizers , best was the ostentatiously named &amp;ldquo ; RR &amp;mdash ; Grill 41 signature steak tartare&amp;rdquo ; ( $21 ) , which was roughly chopped , adequately seasoned and enjoyable , although I&amp;rsquo ; d say that its ingredients could have sung a little louder . Bear in mind , too , that there are slightly cheaper tartares in town that by comparison make you say &amp;ldquo ; Wow ! &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23424;TOOLONG ... title= " Beef tartare at Grill 41 " alt= " Beef tartare at Grill 41 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;23460;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1549968 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; We were perplexed by the sea of Granny Smith apple emulsion that almost drowned four seared scallops ( $19 ) . Dry and flavour-deprived &amp;ldquo ; RR&amp;rdquo ; grilled octopus was a big letdown ( $18 ) that made us scrape the plate for the meagre consolation of burnt honey . The menu also mentione pork belly being a component of the dish , but it was MIA . The &amp;ldquo ; RR&amp;rdquo ; house beet salad ( $18 ) seemed off-puttingly thrown-together , made with slow-roasted squash that felt tired and an alarming amount of fris&amp;eacute ; e. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23490;TOOLONG ... title= " Scallops with Granny Smith apple emulsion at Grill 41 in the Lord Elgin Hotel " alt= " Scallops with Granny Smith apple emulsion at Grill 41 in the Lord Elgin Hotel " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;23526;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1549850 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23556;TOOLONG ... title= " Octopus appetizer at Grill 41 in the Lord Elgin Hotel " alt= " Octopus appetizer at Grill 41 in the Lord Elgin Hotel " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;23592;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1549855 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wild mushroom risotto ( $22 and not an &amp;ldquo ; RR&amp;rdquo ; dish ) was massively portioned and acceptable , but fell short of the more flavourful and al-dente rice treat I can make for myself . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;24274;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1548218 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Just because Ottawa chef Marc Lepine won the Canadian Culinary Championships twice doesn&amp;rsquo ; t mean he would be cocky about his chances were he competing once more this weekend . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m sure it just gets harder every year , the competition , &amp;rdquo ; says Lepine , chef-owner of Atelier , the cutting-edge tasting-menu restaurant on Rochester Street . After winning qualifying competitions in Ottawa , Lepine took home gold at the national level in 2012 and 2016 , and is the only Canadian chef to have won twice at the championships . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Held in Kelowna for many years , the championships have moved to Ottawa , and its first edition in the capital will be held this weekend . A slate of events will culminate in Saturday night&amp;rsquo ; s grand finale competition at the Shaw Centre . There , a dozen Canadian chefs who won the qualifying competitions in their cities , including Ottawa qualifier Ian Carswell of the Black Tartan Kitchen in Carleton Place , will serve their best dishes to a panel of judges and the public . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The grand finale , which is sold out , raises funds for three causes benefitting young Canadians &amp;mdash ; B2ten , which bolsters amateur sport , MusiCounts , which supports music education , and Community Food Centres Canada , which assists low-income communities through food . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thanks to photos on Instagram and detailed descriptions , Lepine was able to size up this year&amp;rsquo ; s grand finale entrants . The edited conversation below is his take on the field and the competition . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;24304;TOOLONG ... title= " Ian Carswell prepared Milkhouse Lamb at the Ottawa regionals for the 2020 Canadian Culinary Championships . " alt= " Ian Carswell prepared Milkhouse Lamb at the Ottawa regionals for the 2020 Canadian Culinary Championships . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;24340;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1548219 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What 's the first thing that strikes you about these dishes ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Everything is just more artistic-looking . People are putting a lot more attention to detail in their presentations . There&amp;rsquo ; s flow to some of these plates , and they&amp;rsquo ; re colourful . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s not like it used to be . Previously , people didn&amp;rsquo ; t put quite as much emphasis on the way the plate looked . It was more about making sure all the flavours were working really well together . And then once you had all those ingredients put together , presentation always seemed like the last thing . " data-portal-copyright= " Peter Hum " **28;24823;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1540064 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Chef has asked me to ask you if you would like to be cooked for , &amp;rdquo ; our grey-suited server asked us &amp;mdash ; rather euphemistically , it should be added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Had that low-key representative of the much-lauded Los Angeles restaurant Providence been more blunt , he would have said : &amp;ldquo ; Would you like us to pamper you with what will likely be one of the best and most luxurious seafood-centred meals of your lives , with freshly shaved white truffles imported from Italy , sprinklings of caviar and top-grade A5 Wagyu beef helping to make dinner more delicious and memorable ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Either way , the answer from my food-loving friends and me could only have been yes . When we visited the 14-year-old Melrose Avenue fine-dining destination last fall , we wanted nothing less than to have Providence&amp;rsquo ; s chef and co-owner Michael Cimarusti pull out the stops with a 10-course tasting menu that proffered a succession of flawlessly prepared delicacies. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For three days in Los Angeles and nearby Pasadena , our itinerary was geared almost single-mindedly on eating , from tacos to truffles with as much as possible in between , and our final night&amp;rsquo ; s dinner at Providence was practically preordained to be a highlight . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;24853;TOOLONG ... title= " Provdence in Los Angeles " alt= " Provdence in Los Angeles " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;24889;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1535927 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;24919;TOOLONG ... title= " The dining room of ProvIdence in Los Angeles " alt= " The dining room of ProvIdence in Los Angeles " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;24955;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1541399 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; We had taken many cues and made reservations based on the counsel of the Michelin Guide California 2019 guidebook . After a 10-year hiatus , the globally recognized taste-making publication last year resumed assessing Southern California&amp;rsquo ; s dining scene , complementing its ongoing scrutiny of the San Francisco area&amp;rsquo ; s eateries. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of the 657 restaurants that received either highly coveted stars or lesser shout-outs in the Michelin guide for the state , Providence was one of just six LA restaurants to receive two stars , repeating its achievement in the 2009 Michelin Guide for Los Angeles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last year and in past years , no LA restaurant received Michelin&amp;rsquo ; s supreme accolade of three stars , given to top-notch restaurants that score highest according to the guidebooks&amp;rsquo ; five criteria : quality of ingredients , mastery of flavour and cooking , personality of the chef in his cuisine , value for money and consistency between visits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At Providence , we were delighted by courses such as sashimi of Japanese Amberjack belly with shaved white truffle , morsels of sea urchin and box crab under an feather-light canopy of scallop mousseline and caviar , and poached antenna of Santa Barbara spiny lobster paired with a Thai-style spiny lobster curry . Risotto with truffles and a lozenge of seared , richly marbled Wagyu brought our parade of savoury dishes to an end , before the sweet finish of torchon of dulce de leche and chocolate , accented with macerated grapes and partnered with pistachio-lacquered brioche and brie sorbet . That dessert even played with our heads by cheekily and uncannily evoking foie gras , which is banned in California . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;24985;TOOLONG ... title= " Spiny lobster curry , a course at Providence in Los Angeles last fall . " alt= " Spiny lobster curry , a course at Providence in Los Angeles last fall . " data-portal-copyright= " Peter Hum " **28;25021;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1540064 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;25051;TOOLONG ... title= " Amadai ( japanese sweet sea bream ) with kabocha squash , chorizo broth , green onion at Providence in Los Angeles " alt= " Amadai ( japanese sweet sea bream ) with kabocha squash , chorizo broth , green onion at Providence in Los Angeles " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;25087;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1540061 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; As fastidiously crafted as our dishes at Providence were , alternatives were prepared for the vegetarian and gluten-abstainer at our table . The restaurant&amp;rsquo ; s setting was elegant , with soft classic jazz wafting through the air , but the experience was neither intimidating or pretentious . Stretching to about four hours , dinner nonetheless felt perfectly paced , with neither lulls nor scrambles marring its flow . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But then , perfection ought to be the reward when dinner , including wines , tip and taxes , topped $440 U.S. per person . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During our trip , we also enjoyed more affordable but substantial satisfactions at restaurants that had received a single star from Michelin , and at some of the budget-friendly designations from the **34;25117;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At Le Comptoir in LA&amp;rsquo ; s Koreatown neighbourhood , chef Gary Menes served an elevated vegetable-inspired tasting menu to a full and cosy house of just 10 people , showcasing impeccable produce grown in his Long Beach garden . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The night that we were at Le Comptoir , which opened five years ago and which has one Michelin star , an additional treat was the understated presence of a certain limelight-shunning celebrity who shall go unnamed , because otherwise John Wick might have to kill me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;25153;TOOLONG ... title= " Chefs at work at Le Comptoir in Los Angeles , a 10-seat restaurant with one Michelin star . Photo credit : Emma Choo , @vancouverfoodie " alt= " Chefs at work at Le Comptoir in Los Angeles , a 10-seat restaurant with one Michelin star . Photo credit : Emma Choo , @vancouverfoodie " data-portal-copyright= " Emma Choo , @vancouverfoodie " **28;25189;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1535925 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; We also ate at the one-Michelin-star restaurant Orsa &amp;amp ; Winston in downtown LA , where chef-owner Joseph Centeno serves Asian-Italian tasting menus at dinner . A tip for gourmets who scrimp and save : you can try the food here and at some other Michelin-starred restaurants at lunch , as we did , and still feel you had something special , such as the pear and apple salad with endive , marcona almonds and nori vinaigrette , which we had , or the chicken katsu with black truffle , which I wish we had had . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In fact , we only grazed at Orsa &amp;amp ; Winston because we visited it as part of a Michelin-themed downtown LA walking tour , led by Avital Food Tours&amp;rsquo ; effervescent guide Penny Truitt. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Our tour made additional stops at two more casual places , pasta specialists Maccheroni Republic , for bianchi and neri pasta and spaghetti ai quattro , and the funky Indian eatery Badmaash , for chocolate chai pot de creme , which with our bewitching goodness miraculously made us feel ravenous again . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Both of these restaurants are so-called &amp;ldquo ; Bib Gourmand&amp;rdquo ; eateries in the eyes of Michelin , meaning that the company&amp;rsquo ; s anonymous inspectors regard them as favourites for delivering good value . Introduced in 1955 , the Bib Gourmand designation is defined as a tip of the hat to worthy restaurants where you can get two courses and a glass of wine or a dessert for $40 or less , excluding tax and tip . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Just last year , Michelin launched a new designation called the Michelin Plate , which sits between stars and Bib Gourmand kudos and acknowledges restaurants that serve very good food and might well move up to receiving a star in following years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Pasadena , we enjoyed ourselves immensely at the fun and un-fussy Michelin-Plated restaurant Union . Persimmon salad and endive salad kicked off our epic dinner , pastas such as pork ragu and squid ink lumache with lobster continued the charge and milk-braised lamb shoulder delivered the final savoury blow . Our desserts , olive oil cake and luscious tiramisu , disappeared quickly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;25219;TOOLONG ... title= " Milk-braised lamb shoulder at Union in Pasadena " alt= " Milk-braised lamb shoulder at Union in Pasadena " data-portal-copyright= " Peter Hum " **28;25255;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1535984 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; We even started off each day with Michelin-Plated breakfasts. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the Raymond 1886 , a former 1930s cottage converted into an outstanding bar and homey restaurant in Pasadena , we fortified ourselves with fried chicken and waffles with red eye gravy , lobster on avocado toast , Nutella French toast and more before heading out on a walking tour of the picturesque City of Roses . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;25285;TOOLONG ... title= " Pasadena 's Colorado Bridge . If we liked Destroyer , Kahn said , we really needed to dine at Vespertine , his controversial fine-dining restaurant down the street . During highly conceptual , outside-the-box meals at Vespertine , Kahn&amp;rsquo ; s futuristic , edible creations can resemble abstract art more than food . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not a restaurant , it&amp;rsquo ; s a portal , &amp;rdquo ; Kahn , who is famously cryptic , said of Vespertine. &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s very powerful and beautiful and interesting . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For corroboration , we looked to the Michelin Guide . It awarded two stars to Vespertine . That cinched it . Vespertine in 2020 or bust . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;EVEN FINE-DINING FANS NEED TACO BREAKS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When I and my fellow gourmands visited Los Angeles , we also went out of our way for tacos &amp;mdash ; and it wasn&amp;rsquo ; t even Tuesday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In fact , it was Sunday &amp;mdash ; the day of the week when Smorgasburg , a massive open-air food market draws thousands to a recently revitalized district of downtown Los Angeles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;25483;TOOLONG ... title= " The scene at Smorgasburg LA , open-air food market in downtown Los Angeles . More info : &lt;a href= " http : //dineLA.com " &gt;dineLA.com&lt;/a &; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;25617;TOOLONG " **32;25644;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumFri , 24 Jan 2020 15:24:44 **45;25678;TOOLONG ... popularity of Ottawa 's Chinese food is at an apex -- and options have never been more diversehttp : **33;25725;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;25760;TOOLONG ... title= " Hang Yu of Harbin Restaurant .
