NewsNationalDining Out : 1 Elgin , the revitalized NAC restaurant , scores with Indigenous-inspired fall menuhttp : **36;47119;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;47157;TOOLONG ... title= " Pan-seared duck breast at 1 Elgin , the recently rebranded restaurant in the National Arts Centre " alt= " Pan-seared duck breast at 1 Elgin , the recently rebranded restaurant in the National Arts Centre " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47193;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480545 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;1 Elgin&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; The former Le Caf&amp;eacute ; inside the National Arts Centre , 613 594-5127 , &lt;a href= " http : //nac-cna.ca/en/1elgin " &gt;nac-cna ... &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Open : &lt;/strong&gt; Tuesday to Saturday 11:30 a.m. to 2 p.m. and 5 to 9 p.m. , closed Sunday and Monday &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Prices : &lt;/strong&gt; starters $13 to $19 , mains $28 to $42 &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Access : &lt;/strong&gt; steps down to entrance &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For four decades , Le Caf&amp;eacute ; , the National Arts Centre&amp;rsquo ; s restaurant , won over innumerable fans . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Its first chef , the late and revered Kurt Waldele , was a pioneer of elevated cuisine that celebrated Canada , years before waving our flag in the kitchen became common . With its unbeatable downtown location and view of the Rideau Canal , Le Caf&amp;eacute ; was a prime destination for locals and tourists alike . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That said , Le Caf&amp;eacute ; also had its detractors . In 2010 , my predecessor Anne DesBrisay wrote : &amp;ldquo ; For as many years as I&amp;rsquo ; ve been writing about Ottawa restaurants&amp;rdquo ; &amp;mdash ; which was 17 at the time &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; I have found the food at the National Arts Centre&amp;rsquo ; s dining room pretty so-what-ish &amp;hellip ; It seemed to me a restaurant stubbornly determined not to outshine the shows going on above its head . &amp;rdquo ; I was of a similar mind in 2013 , although DesBrisay and I were reviewing restaurants overseen by different chefs. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since then , much has changed . In the summer of 2017 , Kenton Leier came on board as the NAC&amp;rsquo ; s executive chef after helming kitchens at some of Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s top downtown hotels . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the summer of 2018 , a first phase of renovations revamped the kitchen and brought in new custom-made tables and chairs , installed circular booths along its back wall , and changed the carpeting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In early June this year , the restaurant closed for more renovations . The bar that had been near the entrance was moved to the middle of the dining room , cutting its long , narrow space in half . Just as dramatically , the ceiling has been modernized , swapping in a reflective surface broken up energetically by sleek bars of light . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The NAC also bid adieu to the Le Caf&amp;eacute ; name . I&amp;rsquo ; m not sure I like the new name &amp;mdash ; 1 Elgin &amp;mdash ; more , but as a signal of change , it&amp;rsquo ; s meaningful . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most importantly , based on my visits to Le Caf&amp;eacute ; earlier this year and 1 Elgin last week , I can say that recent changes have done the restaurant a lot of good . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last Friday , which was not a show night at the NAC , we liked the half-full room&amp;rsquo ; s revitalized ambience . The centralized bar adds more buzz to the place . Over all , the room feels more of today , in line with the NAC&amp;rsquo ; s overall renovation in recent years that coincided with Canada&amp;rsquo ; s sesquicentennial and the centre&amp;rsquo ; s 50th anniversary this year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most dishes we ordered from the menu of six appetizers , six mains and seven desserts were more well made , better presented and even more significant than what I&amp;rsquo ; d eaten at the NAC both years ago and this spring , before Le Caf&amp;eacute ; closed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The extra significance was due to the fact that Leier last month teamed up with Six Nations chef Rich Francis to design the menu . Francis is the first of four resident chefs at the NAC in 2019-20 . His food debuted in mid-September , coinciding with the launch of the NAC&amp;rsquo ; s new Indigenous Theatre , and will be offered at 1 Elgin until Nov. 13 . Francis has set the bar high for the chefs that will have residencies next January , March and May to complete the NAC&amp;rsquo ; s inaugural resident chefs program . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Francis&amp;rsquo ; s input has added , to varying degrees , Indigenous touches or back stories to some menu dishes , and we leaned in that direction , passing on more conventional items such as beef tartare or beef tenderloin that might have been on Le Caf&amp;eacute ; &amp;rsquo ; s menu . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of three appetizers , we enjoyed most of all the &amp;ldquo ; three sisters soup&amp;rdquo ; ( $13 ) . While I&amp;rsquo ; ve since read that three sisters soup usually includes corn , beans and squash , our soup was a hearty , homey potato-fennel soup , enlivened by tender shreds of smoked duck , black olive tapenade and some hidden but zippy candied lemon zest . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47223;TOOLONG ... title= " Three Sisters Soup at 1 Elgin " alt= " Three Sisters Soup at 1 Elgin " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47259;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480518 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Anishinaabe wild rice and Tuscarora corn salad ( $ &lt;span class= " price " &gt;15 ) was simple but refined , with ribbons of lightly pickled root veg and a creamy , intriguing vinaigrette adding breadth to the dish . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47289;TOOLONG ... title= " wild rice and corn salad at 1 Elgin " alt= " wild rice and corn salad at 1 Elgin " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47325;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480544 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Medicine-cured salmon&amp;rdquo ; ( $19 ) was the night&amp;rsquo ; s only dish that felt like a bit of a letdown . Its slab of fish was pleasant and restrained of flavour , but its greens were more pedestrian . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47355;TOOLONG ... title= " Medicine-cured salmon and greens at 1 Elgin " alt= " Medicine-cured salmon and greens at 1 Elgin " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47391;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480543 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Also , when we asked our server why the dish was &amp;ldquo ; medicine-cured , &amp;rdquo ; his answer was more improvised than informed . He returned later to tell us that the salmon had been cured with juniper and beet juice , which was nice to know , but still didn&amp;rsquo ; t answer the question . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On the whole , our servers that night were friendly , attentive and engaged . But they could also have been more knowledgeable about dishes that deserved a bit of explanation and detailed touting. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Main courses were satisfying and attractively plated . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My wife&amp;rsquo ; s Arctic char ( $29 ) was the largest piece of that fish I&amp;rsquo ; d ever seen on a plate , and it was appealingly crisp-skinned and succulent . Wild rice and steel-cut oat risotto struck a comforting note and well-roasted chunky vegetables ( a feature on every plate ) added bulk and visual appeal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47421;TOOLONG ... title= " Arctic char with wild rice and steel-cut oats risotto , at 1 Elgin " alt= " Arctic char with wild rice and steel-cut oats risotto , at 1 Elgin " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47457;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480548 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Elk osso buco ( $42 ) was massive , meaty and duskily-flavoured , and its roasted grapes were a nice accent . However , the marrowbone on the plate was seemingly more for show than enjoyment , as its marrow was dry and didn&amp;rsquo ; t provide the requisite indulgent note . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47487;TOOLONG ... title= " Elk osso bucco with br ? l ? ed marrowbone , at 1 Elgin " alt= " Elk osso bucco with br ? l ? ed marrowbone , at 1 Elgin " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47523;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480547 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pan-seared and impeccably seasoned duck breast ( $32 ) could not have been improved upon . Our table&amp;rsquo ; s vegan was pleased with a colourful mushroom-based main ( $28 ) , supported by surprisingly palatable seitan &amp;ldquo ; prosciutto , &amp;rdquo ; a saffron coconut sauce and pumpkin pur&amp;eacute ; e. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47553;TOOLONG ... title= " Mushrooms with seitan " prosciutto , " saffron coconut sauce and vegetables at 1 Elgin " alt= " Mushrooms with seitan " prosciutto , " saffron coconut sauce and vegetables at 1 Elgin " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47589;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480546 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Because we let 1 Elgin know in advance about birthday celebrants at our table , several appropriately decorated desserts were on the house . Tops was the dark chocolate tart ( $12 ) , especially with its sweet and grassy dollop of sweetgrass ice cream . Maple pumpkin spice cake ( $11 ) did less for us. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47619;TOOLONG ... title= " Dark chocolate tart with sweetgrass ice cream and bannock crumble at 1 Elgin " alt= " Dark chocolate tart with sweetgrass ice cream and bannock crumble at 1 Elgin " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47655;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480550 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47685;TOOLONG ... title= " Maple Pumpkin dessert at One Elgin , pic by Peter Hum " alt= " Maple Pumpkin dessert at One Elgin , pic by Peter Hum " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47721;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480549 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since we were told when we arrived about those free desserts , we allocated that part of the budget on house cocktails ( $11 ) that used Canadian gin and were suitably complex and stiff . Some craft beers are on tap , and the wine list is lengthy , with most bottles in the $40 to $80 range and many wines available by the glass in five- and eight-ounce pours . To support the menu by Francis and Leier , 1 Elgin is also offering wines from Okanagan Valley&amp;rsquo ; s NK&amp;rsquo ; MIP Cellars , Canada&amp;rsquo ; s first Indigenous winery , although the menu consistently refers to &amp;ldquo ; MK&amp;rsquo ; MIP Cellars . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I won&amp;rsquo ; t dwell on the meals I had at Le Caf&amp;eacute ; this spring , except to say I liked them less because they seemed to have been prepared with less attentiveness and were more old-fashioned in terms of taste and appearance . Better dishes included a veal chop special and the beef tenderloin tartare , and the latter is still on the latest menu . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47751;TOOLONG ... title= " Duck confit at Le Cafe , spring 2019 " alt= " Duck confit at Le Cafe , spring 2019 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47787;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480542 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47817;TOOLONG ... title= " Veal chop special at NAC 's Le Cafe , spring 2019 " alt= " Veal chop special at NAC 's Le Cafe , spring 2019 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47853;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480541 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47883;TOOLONG ... title= " Beef tenderloin tartare at NAC 's Le Caf ? , spring 2019 " alt= " Beef tenderloin tartare at NAC 's Le Caf ? , spring 2019 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47919;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480538 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47949;TOOLONG ... title= " Scallops and pork belly at Le Caf ? , spring 2019 " alt= " Scallops and pork belly at Le Caf ? , spring 2019 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;47985;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480537 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;48015;TOOLONG ... title= " Seafood chowder at Le Cafe , spring 2019 " alt= " Seafood chowder at Le Cafe , spring 2019 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;48051;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1480523 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Soon after Leier was hired , he told this newspaper he wanted to raise the level of the food at the NAC&amp;rsquo ; s restaurant , which had received mixed reviews online . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The goal is to be a great restaurant , not an average one , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; It won&amp;rsquo ; t happen overnight , but the effort will be there . &amp;rdquo ; Consistency , he said , was an issue , especially given that on show nights , 150 to 200 guests come for a quick meal before a Southam Hall concert . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Leier is on the right track , I think , with 1 Elgin&amp;rsquo ; s freshened surroundings and the best fare that he and Francis presented persuasively winning us over . We&amp;rsquo ; ll hope that the executive chef and future resident chefs keep up the good work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;48081;TOOLONG " **32;48108;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;48142;TOOLONG ... Hum 's restaurant reviews&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumWed , 09 Oct 2019 15:00:12 **45;48177;TOOLONG ... Food ReviewsFrom Michelin-starred plates to hot dogs , Chicago 's food satisfiedhttp : **31;48224;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;48257;TOOLONG ... title= " A fanciful culinary creation at Smyth , a restaurant with two Michelin stars in Chicago " alt= " A fanciful culinary creation at Smyth , a restaurant with two Michelin stars in Chicago " data-portal-copyright= " Galdones Photography " **28;48293;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1477946 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the last decade , Michelin-starred fine dining in Chicago has become practically as iconic for food-lovers as the city&amp;rsquo ; s famed hot dogs , Italian beef sandwiches and deep-dish pizza . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since the Michelin Guide began surveying sleek dishes in Chicago in 2011 , more than 40 restaurants in the city , from the world-famous avant-garde temple of gastronomy Alinea down , have been awarded much-coveted stars . The latest Michelin Guide for the city , released in late September , awards one or more stars to 25 restaurants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While I didn&amp;rsquo ; t make it to three-starred Alinea on my recent trip to Chicago , I ate terrifically at several fine-dining destinations and neighbourhood restaurants alike . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the two-Michelin-starred Smyth , a warm and gorgeous three-year-old restaurant in the West Loop that specializes in sleek tasting menus , the open kitchen turned out a succession of fascinating dishes made with ingredients from its dedicated farm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;48323;TOOLONG ... title= " Chefs at work at Smyth , a restaurant in Chicago with two Michelin stars " alt= " Chefs at work at Smyth , a restaurant in Chicago with two Michelin stars " data-portal-copyright= " Eugene ( Huge ) Galdones " **28;48359;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1477967 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Deconstructed gazpacho , caramelized halibut with double cream and toasted crab and aged lamb with grapes , garlic and a beef-fat brioche thrilled with refined flavours and precise technique . Recondite signature desserts combined milk chocolate ganache with seaweed oil and even bits of shiitake mushroom , or candied salted egg yolk with frozen yogurt meringue . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;48389;TOOLONG ... title= " Milk chocolate ganache with seawood , strawberry and shiitake mushroom , a fanciful culinary creation at Smyth , a restaurant in Chicago " alt= " Milk chocolate ganache with seawood , strawberry and shiitake mushroom , a fanciful culinary creation at Smyth , a restaurant in Chicago " data-portal-copyright= " Eugene ( Huge ) Galdones " **28;48425;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1477943 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Less outr&amp;eacute ; but still deeply satisfying was a dinner at Sepia , a sophisticated West Loop spot with one Michelin star . There , succulent King salmon with white asparagus , rhubarb , sorrel , cashews and coconut , as well as slices of supremely beefy Wagyu tri-tip with Asian pear , maitake mushrooms and cabbages , were delightful main courses . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;48455;TOOLONG ... title= " Wagyu beef tri-tip at Sepia in Chicago " alt= " Wagyu beef tri-tip at Sepia in Chicago " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;48491;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1478026 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Further north , in Lincoln Park , we enjoyed a deluxe dinner at the more casual but still one-Michelin-starred Boka . There , dry-aged duck breast with impeccably crispy skin was the stunner among many fine main courses . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;48521;TOOLONG ... title= " Dry-aged duck breast at Boka in Chicago " alt= " Dry-aged duck breast at Boka in Chicago " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;48557;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1478027 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The hip Logan Square neighbourhood was worth a food-focused visit , thanks to the marvellous pork cutlet breakfast sandwich , beet bruschetta and epic carrot cake at Lula Caf&amp;eacute ; , a beloved farm-to-table haunt . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;48587;TOOLONG ... title= " carrot cake at Lula Cafe in Chicago " alt= " carrot cake at Lula Cafe in Chicago " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;48623;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1478029 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Not far away , the funky , James Beard Award-winning eatery Fat Rice served some exceptional and unique Asian food including deeply savoury pork dumplings , massive chilli prawns and piri-piri chicken that seethed with incendiary goodness . What&amp;rsquo ; s more , around the corner from the Bakery at Fat Rice , where magnificent egg tarts and other baked treats can be bought to go . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;48653;TOOLONG ... title= " Piri Piri chicken at Fat Rice in Chicago " alt= " Piri Piri chicken at Fat Rice in Chicago " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;48689;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1477948 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lunch at the Publican , a meat-forward , beer-hall-like place near the Fulton Market , started with a revelatory selection of top-notch hams , followed by massive portions of mussels and fries and the gastropub&amp;rsquo ; s famed roast chicken with fries . Don&amp;rsquo ; t miss pastry chef Erika Chan&amp;rsquo ; s swoon-worthy desserts. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;48719;TOOLONG ... title= " Chicken and fries at the Publican in Chicago " alt= " Chicken and fries at the Publican in Chicago " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;48755;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1478042 " /&gt; Gusto Worldwide Media reboots Cook Like A Chef TV showhttp : **36;49221;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;49259;TOOLONG ... title= " Chef Katie Ardington. " alt= " Chef Katie Ardington. " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;49295;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1191270 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa-based food network Gusto Worldwide Media is producing a new version of the series Cook Like A Chef , which originated 20 years ago and ran internationally for six seasons . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The original series bolstered the careers of Canadian chefs such as Michael Bonacini and Ned Bell , as well as Ottawa-area chefs Rene Rodriguez , Michael Cummings and Georges Laurier . More than 160 episodes were filmed , each dedicated to a single ingredient with a chef explaining cooking techniques , tips and tricks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Episodes of the original series still appear on the international food channel Gusto TV and can be streamed in the U.S. , United Kingdom , Latin America and Singapore . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The new version , now in production , will feature four chefs : Katie Ardington , executive chef of the Ottawa-based Beckta restaurant group and formerly the personal chef to Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and his family ; Montreal-based chefs Derek Dammann , owner of Maison Publique , and Natalia Machado ; and Toronto chef Craig Wong of the restaurant Patois Toronto . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shot in Gusto&amp;rsquo ; s east-end Ottawa studio , the new series will be available internationally on Gusto TV and the CTV Life Channel next year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;49325;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;49360;TOOLONG ... NewsDining Out : Alice in Little Italy is a trailblazer , and should be recognized nationallyhttp : **30;50847;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;50879;TOOLONG ... title= " Briana Kim at Alice Restaurant on Adeline Street in Little Italy . " alt= " Briana Kim at Alice Restaurant on Adeline Street in Little Italy . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;50915;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1462198 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;50945;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; 40 Adeline St. , 613-733-0707 , &lt;a href= " http : //alicerestaurant.ca " &gt;alicerest ... &lt;br&gt; Open : Tuesday to Saturday 5:30 to 9:30 p.m. , closed Sunday and Monday &lt;br&gt; Prices : tasting menu $95 per person &lt;br&gt; Access : one step to gravelled area , steps with handrail to front door &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The very first intrigue at Alice , the uniquely vegetable-focused fine-dining restaurant that chef-owner Briana Kim opened in June , involves assuring yourself that you have come to the right address . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Hers is the place on a modest residential side street in Little Italy where marc kitchen , and before that The Rex , had been . Kim , the self-taught , award-winning chef who represented Ottawa at the 2018 Canadian Culinary Championships , now presides inside a converted house with a new wood fa ? ade and a mini-greenhouse in front , but no sign of the restaurant 's name outside . &lt;/span&gt; To be clear , Alice is not the neighbouring property with an InfoWars sticker on its door , which has its own mysteries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;50981;TOOLONG ... title= " Briana Kim with some of her dishes at Alice Restaurant on Adeline Street in Little Italy . The exterior of the restaurant . " alt= " Briana Kim with some of her dishes at Alice Restaurant on Adeline Street in Little Italy . The exterior of the restaurant . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;51017;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1462204 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; When you enter Alice , the questions mount . Above all : What&amp;rsquo ; s in those jars ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One wall of Alice&amp;rsquo ; s front dining area is a clear cabinet filled with almost three dozen jars with oddly hued contents . Looking more closely , you discover that they contain the slowly fermenting materials of Kim&amp;rsquo ; s cutting-edge cuisine &amp;mdash ; miso pastes made with sweet peas , chickpeas or sesame , vinegar-based creations involving crabapple flowers , Thai basil or spruce tips , concoctions made with jalape&amp;ntilde ; o , morels , reindeer moss and even pine cones . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fine-dining fans will know that fermentation is all the rage in the world&amp;rsquo ; s top kitchens , from global leader Noma in Copenhagen down . With her jars , Kim shows she has gone all-in on fermentation as she takes her culinary artistry to the next level . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kim&amp;rsquo ; s previous and more casual restaurant , Caf&amp;eacute ; My House in Hintonburg , laid five years of groundwork for Alice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But where Caf&amp;eacute ; My House , which Kim closed in January , was funky and dark , Alice , which seats 20 or so in its cosy , L-shaped , white-and-birch-coloured space , is ascetically spare . Only its jar-filled cabinet , a more artful wood wall that celebrates flowers in the rear dining area , the sleek bar that dispenses pricey but top-notch cocktails and the hubbub in the open kitchen distract from Kim&amp;rsquo ; s rarefied dishes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And where Caf&amp;eacute ; My House&amp;rsquo ; s plant-based offerings included brunches on weekends and five-course tasting menus at dinner , Alice aims higher , serving just an eight-course , $95 tasting menu that can be paired with natural wines or alcohol-free house-made beverages for $60 . ( Cocktails , Burdock beer and Revel cider are also available. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , the investment and stakes are high for Kim&amp;rsquo ; s most uncompromising project to date . I can say , though , after my meal there Saturday night , that Alice served a singular and fascinating dinner that surpassed two tasting-menu experiences I had had at Caf&amp;eacute ; My House . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her food is supremely refined and arguably even virtuous , applying an ambitious chef&amp;rsquo ; s devotion to highly creative and technical culinary transformations in the service of veganism and locavorism . The results are frequently visually stunning , marvellously thoughtful and not only delicious but deliciously novel . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Our dinner at Alice began with bread and snacks , with each counting as a course . But Kim&amp;rsquo ; s approach made clear that Alice means to transport guests to a culinary wonderland . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Slices of warm , perfect sourdough came with a candle , which turned out to be &amp;ldquo ; butter&amp;rdquo ; made from creamy fermented rice , which was softening thanks to a burning walnut &amp;ldquo ; wick . &amp;rdquo ; For snacks , servers brought something scarcely cooked ( a lightly charred summer radish , complete with its leaf , with cranberry bean miso that had been aged for three months ) and an exquisite little pastry ( a toasted sunflower seed and star anise butter tart with compressed plums and anise flowers ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Next came a bowl , and a table-side flourish . A sphere of coconut yogurt nestled with cranberry beans , and smoked , toasted and salted coconut flakes in a savoury broth . Kim then topped the dish with spoonfuls of an apparently supercooled powder flavoured with yuzu , the Japanese citrus fruit . Vapour , or probably nitrogen gas , billowed from the bowl . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As showy as the bowl was , it was even tastier . Bite after bite , it provided a refreshing play of sweetness , citrus , saltiness , textures and temperatures . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;51047;TOOLONG ... title= " The dish seen here is Coconut , Cranberry Beans and Coffee . " alt= " The dish seen here is Coconut , Cranberry Beans and Coffee . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;51083;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1462201 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alice&amp;rsquo ; s elegant and visually arresting salad course will be very hard to displace from my memory . Kim had arranged assorted greens from Juniper Farms in a mini-bouquet , topped it with toasted flaxseed , other small , good things , and offset it with a ring of kohlrabi filled with sea buckthorn jelly . The salad&amp;rsquo ; s dressing was fermented house-made almond milk , added in another table-side manoeuvre . The dish was simply revelatory. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;51113;TOOLONG ... title= " The dish seen here is Summer Bouquet . " alt= " The dish seen here is Summer Bouquet . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;51149;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1462202 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The next two courses were increasingly savoury . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; First came a geometric arrangement of circles and squares that starred cherry tomatoes , precisely topped with a red pepper-jalapeno salsa , lacto-fermented basil and toasted freekeh , contrasted with a crisp , perforated smoked garlic chip and a ponzu-flavoured gel , as well as a fennel-spiced &amp;ldquo ; butter&amp;rdquo ; powder . If I&amp;rsquo ; m right , the dish also included just enough subtle Sichuan-pepper-based oil to leave the faintest tingle on the tongue . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;51179;TOOLONG ... title= " The dish seen here is Tomato and Ponzu. " alt= " The dish seen here is Tomato and Ponzu. " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;51215;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1462217 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eggplant was the star of the final savoury course , cooked so as to coax out its meaty mouthfeel . The slabs of eggplant were garnished with a variety of pickles and came with a deeply flavoured cucumber-based sauce . Nudging the dish over the top was a crisp ribbon that packed crunch and umami , I believe from a dusting of sea-vegetable powder . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;51245;TOOLONG ... title= " Eggplant with cucumber sauce at Alice " alt= " Eggplant with cucumber sauce at Alice " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;51281;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1462219 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; With these dishes , I had Alice&amp;rsquo ; s alcohol-free pairings and was struck by their quality and even ingenuity . Among those drinks were glasses or cups of blackberry , hibiscus and mint kombucha , lime leaf lemonade , a warm , clear , super-savoury tomato tea , and a cool cucumber-ginger-cilantro tonic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The first of two desserts combined house-made silken tofu with viscous elderberry honey and a scattering of fresh and freeze dried strawberries . It was good on its own but better still with its pairing , the strawberry sour topped with a vanilla and tonka bean &amp;ldquo ; meringue . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;51311;TOOLONG ... title= " Strawberry , silken tofu and elderflower honey dessert at Alice " alt= " Strawberry , silken tofu and elderflower honey dessert at Alice " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;51347;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1462218 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The knockout dessert was the kitchen&amp;rsquo ; s riff on an ice cream sandwich , that placed a quenelle of fermented-rice-based &amp;ldquo ; ice cream&amp;rdquo ; between shards of hyper-crisp oat cake , buttressed by berries in a charred pine cone syrup . Although I&amp;rsquo ; m no fan of licorice , the licorice anise soda paired well with the dessert . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;51377;TOOLONG ... title= " " ice cream sandwich " dessert at Alice " alt= " " ice cream sandwich " dessert at Alice " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;51413;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1462226 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Our meal ended with a mignardise &amp;mdash ; a house-made mint chocolate candy &amp;mdash ; and a keepsake copy of the menu , which abbreviated its descriptions of the dishes . Kim told us before we left that dishes come on and off the menu continually , and that roughly every six weeks there&amp;rsquo ; s a new menu , to the delight of Alice&amp;rsquo ; s repeat customers . Given that long-fermenting ingredients are involved , Kim is already planning winter dishes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In all , Alice packed a striking amount of pleasant stimulation into our 95 minutes there . In fact , it&amp;rsquo ; s possible the kitchen and staff were a little too efficient . Our meal could have felt a touch more relaxed in terms of pacing and delivery , and even more warm . But then , Kim and her team knew once I arrived that I was there in a critical capacity , and perhaps they switched to an overly professional , too-cool mode . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And for all the details they dispensed , Kim and her servers could have told us a bit more about the thinking behind the dishes &amp;mdash ; the &amp;ldquo ; why&amp;rdquo ; as well as the &amp;ldquo ; what . &amp;rdquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve experienced that kind of curated dining at a Michelin-starred place or two , and found it gave a fuller appreciation of the food and the people who made it , enriching our experience and justifying the lofty prices . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , Alice serves notice that Kim is not simply a fine chef on Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s arguably under-appreciated dining scene , but an important culinary trailblazer worthy of recognition nationally and beyond . There are remarkable dishes to be discovered and demystified here now , and I expect there will be many more in the future . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;51443;TOOLONG " **32;51470;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/peterhum " &gt;twitter ... &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumWed , 11 Sep 2019 20:33:52 **45;51504;TOOLONG ... Food ReviewsCanada 's first kosher barbecue cook-off yields delicious winners in Barrhavenhttp : **31;51551;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;51584;TOOLONG ... title= " John Thomson shows off turkey entries at the Kosher BBC Competition at the Ottawa Torah Centre , Sept. 8 , 2019 " alt= " John Thomson shows off turkey entries at the Kosher BBC Competition at the Ottawa Torah Centre , Sept. 8 , 2019 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;51620;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1460815 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Sunday afternoon , Barrhaven once again lived up to its nickname &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; barbecue-haven. &amp;rdquo ; But this time , the event that drew hundreds to the Ottawa Torah Centre was a Canadian first . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The crowd , which included foodies from not just Ottawa but also Montreal , Toronto and New York , came for the first Ottawa Kosher BBQ Cook-Off and Festival , organized by the OTC&amp;rsquo ; s Rabbi Menachem M. Blum . While summer kosher barbecue cook-offs and Jewish food festivals are well-established in the United States , there was no Canadian precedent for the rabbi&amp;rsquo ; s event . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That said , in May , Barrhaven played host to Canada&amp;rsquo ; s biggest barbecue competition , when the fourth annual Capital BBQ Festival drew more than 40 professional barbecue teams from Ontario , Quebec and the Northeastern U.S. , vying to be that festival&amp;rsquo ; s grand champion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Capital BBQ Festival&amp;rsquo ; s organizer , John Thomson , was on hand at Sunday&amp;rsquo ; s kosher event to run its centrepiece competition . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;51650;TOOLONG ... title= " Ottawa pitmaster John Thomson shows off turkey entries to judges at the first Ottawa Kosher BBQ Cook-Off and Festival at the Ottawa Torah Centre on Sept. 8 , 2019. " alt= " Ottawa pitmaster John Thomson shows off turkey entries to judges at the first Ottawa Kosher BBQ Cook-Off and Festival at the Ottawa Torah Centre on Sept. 8 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;51686;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1460815 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sunday&amp;rsquo ; s contest featured seven barbecue teams squaring off in three categories ( chicken , turkey and brisket , all in keeping with a kosher diet ) and submitting their entries to a panel of five judges . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The event also allowed the public to buy tickets to sample the teams&amp;rsquo ; cooking and award a people&amp;rsquo ; s choice award . As well , a kosher food court served pulled brisket sandwiches , corned beef sandwiches , Moroccan burgers , hot dogs , veggie burgers , knishes , fries , salads and drinks as well as popcorn and cotton candy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I was one of the event&amp;rsquo ; s judges , and can tell you that not only is kosher barbecue a thing &amp;mdash ; it&amp;rsquo ; s a delicious thing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I came to the event with the bonafides of having judged during the last five years at more than 20 competitions in Ontario , Quebec and New York state that were sanctioned by the Kansas City Barbecue Society . At those events , chicken and brisket feature , but so do pork ribs and pork shoulder , which can frequently appear as pulled pork . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Naturally , I was keen to see and taste the kosher approach to barbecue , and I along with my fellow judges would apply the same criteria used to assess KCBS entries , scrutinizing each piece of meat for appearance , taste and tenderness . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here&amp;rsquo ; s what I judged in the chicken category : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;51716;TOOLONG ... title= " Chicken entries at Canada 's first kosher barbecue cook-off , held in Barrhaven on Sept. 8/2019 " alt= " Chicken entries at Canada 's first kosher barbecue cook-off , held in Barrhaven on Sept. 8/2019 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;51752;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1460873 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The chicken entries yielded an enjoyably diverse range of flavours . Over the years , KCBS competitions have seen the flavour profiles that teams present narrow practically to the point of homogeneity , and I was happy to see variety . The chicken thigh in the lower left was the most &amp;ldquo ; KCBS&amp;rdquo ; entry in terms of looks and taste , given its sweet , sticky glaze . Other entries were relatively un-sauced and different spices came into play . In 20 KCBS competitions , I&amp;rsquo ; ve never come across a curry-tinged chicken entry like the one on the bottom right , which I nonetheless thought quite highly of . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here are entries in the turkey category : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;51782;TOOLONG ... title= " Turkey entries at the Kosher BBC Competition at the Ottawa Torah Centre , Sept. 8 , 2019 " alt= " Turkey entries at the Kosher BBC Competition at the Ottawa Torah Centre , Sept. 8 , 2019 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;51818;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1460876 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; I was a little surprised not to receive any dark meat in this category , not that I have anything against well-cooked turkey breast . I just think that it might have been easier for dark-meat entries to score higher on tenderness , and indeed , some of these turkey entries were a little dry . The &amp;ldquo ; pulled turkey&amp;rdquo ; was really very good , though , and I also was partial to the entry beside it that went big with roasted garlic and herbs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The competition saved the best for last : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;51848;TOOLONG ... title= " Brisket entries at Canada 's first kosher barbecue competition at the Ottawa Torah Centre on Sept. 8 , 2019 " alt= " Brisket entries at Canada 's first kosher barbecue competition at the Ottawa Torah Centre on Sept. 8 , 2019 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;51884;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1460814 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Beef brisket enjoys a reputation as one of the hardest meats to barbecue well , and when things go wrong , that expensive cut can be rendered inedibly tough and dry . Also , even pro teams at KCBS events can turn in brisket that&amp;rsquo ; s punishingly salty or even bouillon-y . ( The competitors are , it should be said , trying to wow judges who take at most two bites of meat , with punchy , flavour-forward samples. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , the level of brisket at the kosher event was strikingly high . I certainly have had much worse brisket at KCBS events . The best brisket samples on Sunday had notable succulence , fine beefiness and a balance of smoke and seasoning . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We judged our entries without knowing which teams had submitted them , as per the KCBS rules . It was only on Sunday night that I learned that the competition&amp;rsquo ; s grand champion was the Irving Rivers team . In the individual categories , the top finishers were : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chicken : 1st : Coal Nidrei ( Ottawa Jewish Community School ) . 2nd : Big Macher BBQ ( Camp Bnai Brith Ottawa ) . 3rd : Irving Rivers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Turkey : 1st : Big Macher BBQ ( Camp Bnai Brith Ottawa ) . 2nd : Irving Rivers . 3rd : Up in Smoke . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brisket : 1st : Coal Nidrei ( Ottawa Jewish Community School ) . 2nd : Irving Rivers . 3rd : Up in Smoke . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All seven teams this year were from Ottawa . &amp;ldquo ; We had no financial prizes as it was our first year , just recognition with medals and trophies , &amp;rdquo ; Blum said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Congratulations to all who cooked . Trucks are the new family ride . What 's happened to us ? &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumMon , 09 Sep 2019 14:57:59 **45;52080;TOOLONG ... Out : Some pretty dishes bloomed , others wilted at Tulip Restauranthttp : **30;52127;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;52159;TOOLONG ... title= " Cornish hen with polenta at Tulip " alt= " Cornish hen with polenta at Tulip " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;52195;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1451835 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tulip Restaurant &amp; Bar&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; 361 Queen St. ( inside the Hilton Garden Inn Ottawa Downtown ) , 613-234-6363 , &lt;a href= " http : //tulipottawa.com " &gt;tulipottawa. ... &lt;br&gt; **33;52225;TOOLONG : Daily from noon to 2:30 p.m. and 5:30 to 9:30 p.m. , also weekday breakfasts from 6:30 to 10:30 a.m. , weekend breakfasts 7 to 11 a.m. &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Prices : &lt;/strong&gt; appetizers $7.95 to $21.95 , mains $17.95 to $29.95 &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Access : &lt;/strong&gt; no steps to front door , washrooms &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the fall of 2017 , when David Vinoya was the chef of Wild Sage Kitchen &amp;amp ; Bar in Regina , he won that city&amp;rsquo ; s Gold Medal Plates competition after wowing judges with a striking dish that he had enigmatically dubbed &amp;ldquo ; The Nest . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Equal parts still life and small plate , it was , in the words of head judge James Chatto , &amp;ldquo ; sensationally beautiful . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Vinoya&amp;rsquo ; s dish , watercress became a gel . Black olives were turned into powder and beets were made into &amp;ldquo ; soil . &amp;rdquo ; Molecular gastronomy turned chicken into a crisp tuile . The dish&amp;rsquo ; s star was a sphere of ice cream made with the yolks of eggs that had been cured by soaking them for a month in mud and salt , as is done in the Philippines , where Vinoya was born and raised . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These days , Vinoya cooks in Ottawa . Wild Sage was inside a DoubleTree by Hilton hotel , and more than a year ago , Vinoya moved here to become the executive chef at the Hilton Garden Inn Ottawa Downtown , where Tulip Restaurant and Bar lies beyond its Queen Street entrance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This summer , I had two dinners and a lunch at Tulip , hoping for some medal-winning brilliance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tulip&amp;rsquo ; s menus definitely intrigued . Vinoya has a wide-roaming curiosity about food , so that his multicultural menu makes stops in Japan , Italy , China , the Middle East , the Philippines and the rest of Canada , sometimes mashing up influences from here and there . Among the menu&amp;rsquo ; s details are ingredients such as crab , sea urchin , bacon jam , black garlic aioli , and truffle oil &amp;mdash ; the stuff that makes connoisseurs and especially umami-lovers salivate. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In line with Chatto&amp;rsquo ; s kudos , Vinoya&amp;rsquo ; s plating is definitely a strong point . His dishes were usually pretty and exuberant , if on occasion a touch contrived . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But on the whole , our meals were uneven . Some dishes were interesting , solidly made and satisfying . Others were just OK and a few let us down . For too many dishes , some components had little to no impact , making you wonder if simpler food would not have been better . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My second dinner there was markedly my best experience at Tulip , and I wondered if who was cooking in the kitchen is as significant as what we ordered . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At my first visit , a weekday lunch , we had several appetizers that were not as tasty as they looked . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Three steamed pork belly buns ( $11.95 ) were presented like treasures on a black stone slab in a wooden tray , with a small salad and dipping sauce on the side . But visuals aside , the bao buns needed work . The too-dry pork belly sorely lacked succulence . The odd move of dredging the buns in creole seasoning added significant heat , but unpleasantly so . The sweet-salty sauce on the side would have been better inside the bun . Overall , the kitchen&amp;rsquo ; s twists on a classic snack did not improve it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;52260;TOOLONG ... title= " Bao buns at Tulip restaurant in the Hilton Garden Inn on Queen Street , " alt= " Bao buns at Tulip restaurant in the Hilton Garden Inn on Queen Street , " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;52296;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1451340 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spicy tuna ( $13.95 ) arrived atop oblongs of deep-fried rice and , more ostentatiously , on a bed of rocks in its bowl . It was not bad , but would have been better had its rice been less crisp . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;52326;TOOLONG ... title= " Spicy Tuna appetizer at Tulip restaurant in the Hilton Garden Inn on Queen Street " alt= " Spicy Tuna appetizer at Tulip restaurant in the Hilton Garden Inn on Queen Street " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;52362;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1450611 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fried flatbread ( $12.95 ) topped with mushrooms , truffle oil , whipped goat cheese , a cloud of parmesan and pea shoots was tasty , although the bread did feel heavy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;52392;TOOLONG ... title= " Mushroom flatbread at Tulip restaurant in the Hilton Garden Inn on Queen Street " alt= " Mushroom flatbread at Tulip restaurant in the Hilton Garden Inn on Queen Street " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;52428;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1451337 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lunch&amp;rsquo ; s heftiest item was Tulip&amp;rsquo ; s doughnut-burger hybrid ( $18.95 ) , seemingly built for Instagram or for eating on a dare . Perhaps predictably , it was too massive and dulce-de-leche-drizzled to be eaten by hand , which to me is a big point of eating a hamburger . In all , this burger struck me as overladen . ( To be fair , Tulip offers a &amp;ldquo ; standard&amp;rdquo ; burger and six sandwiches that are more streamlined. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;52458;TOOLONG ... title= " Sweet and savoury doughnut burger and salad at Tulip restaurant in the Hilton Garden Inn on Queen Street " alt= " Sweet and savoury doughnut burger and salad at Tulip restaurant in the Hilton Garden Inn on Queen Street " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;52494;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1450567 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; At a weekend dinner , three dishes were meh , while a fourth stood out . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The texture of a large slab of pan-fried falafel ( $14.95 ) varied from cake-y to moist to mushy , and it was a little bland . The accompanying salad , which featured a lemon br&amp;ucirc ; l&amp;eacute ; e peanut chutney , arugula , red cabbage , avocado herb sauce , cured onions and sumac vinaigrette , could have been edited , as not every element sang . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;52524;TOOLONG ... title= " Falafel and salad at Tulip " alt= " Falafel and salad at Tulip " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;52560;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1453857 " /&gt; &lt;div class= " item-title-row " &gt;&lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;Of two mains , best was a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; tasty , if oily , spaghetti dish dubbed " porkuni " ( $23.95 ) . &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; Billed as pasta with bacon , a sea urchin and crab sauce , dried seaweed , herb pistou " jus , " sesame seeds , pork crackling crumbs and nori , this dish too could have been simplified . Decades ago , I was in Morocco for an afternoon . More recently , I spent a few days playing tourist in Cape Town and its surrounding winelands , which some say hardly represents the continent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All that to say , these days I&amp;rsquo ; m feeling I&amp;rsquo ; ve had more revelatory encounters with the cultures of African countries during my visits to Ottawa restaurants that serve their national dishes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most recently , I&amp;rsquo ; ve been eating and enjoying the meat-forward fare from Suya Palace in Centretown , which serves some key Nigerian dishes and especially the grilled items called , as you would guess , suya. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; ve also visited &amp;mdash ; and been pleased by some dishes at &amp;mdash ; Suya Joint/African Grill , which is tucked away in a Clyde Avenue strip mall . There , a chef from Lesotho serves his version of suya , plus the barbecue style known as braai , which is native to South Africa , which happens to encircle Lesotho . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These modest eateries share a dedication to authentic flavours that rely on spices imported from Africa . The dishes I liked most , and even some that I cared less for , were well-seasoned and deeply savoury . It did seem that both restaurants had been discovered by African expats. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Suya Palace , which this spring replaced African Slow Food on Bronson Avenue near Gladstone Avenue , is a tiny place more geared to take-out orders , although it does seat about 10 people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Best here were orders of chicken and beef suya . Both were beguilingly seasoned and tasty , although those with peanut allergies should know that peanuts are usually included in suya marinades. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The chicken was all bone-in , a thigh and two drumsticks , and it was sufficiently moist , if not juicy , after its time on Suya Palace&amp;rsquo ; s charcoal grill . Beef suya was tender , if not moist . Goat suya was flavourful , but its toughness turned eating into exercise for our jaws . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;53626;TOOLONG ... title= " Chicken suya at Suya Palace " alt= " Chicken suya at Suya Palace " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;53662;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1450582 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;53692;TOOLONG ... title= " Beef suya combo with plantain , jollof rice and cole slaw from Suya Palace " alt= " Beef suya combo with plantain , jollof rice and cole slaw from Suya Palace " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;53728;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1450368 " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;53758;TOOLONG ... title= " Goat suya from Suya Palace " alt= " Goat suya from Suya Palace " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;53794;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1450361 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; At Suya Palace&amp;rsquo ; s counter , there&amp;rsquo ; s a small metal bin filled with orange powder . Although the cook that took your order already asked you how spicy you wanted your suya , he will still add a few spoonfuls of that orange powder , which turns out to be a made-in-Nigeria chilli powder that adds some fierce , persistent , swelling heat . Try some . It&amp;rsquo ; s good . But don&amp;rsquo ; t say you weren&amp;rsquo ; t warned . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Less pleasing at Suya Palace was its suya-spiced grilled quarter chicken , only because its white meat was dry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;53824;TOOLONG ... title= " Quarter chicken with plantain from Suya Palace " alt= " Quarter chicken with plantain from Suya Palace " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;53860;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1450364 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; I can recommend Suya Palace&amp;rsquo ; s jollof rice , a Nigerian side dish that was moist , tomato-y , well-seasoned and markedly smoky . Had I simply consulted Wikipedia first , I would have known better . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;53890;TOOLONG ... title= " Ogbonna okra soup at Suya Palace " alt= " Ogbonna okra soup at Suya Palace " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;53926;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1450560 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The restaurant is not licensed . Apart from basic soft drinks , it also offers vitamalt , the non-alcoholic Caribbean malt beverage . Its meat is halal. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At Suya Joint/African Grill , which opened late last year , chef-owner Koele Khutlang , a native of Lesotho , serves his take on suya , which presents its beef , goat , chicken and gizzards in smaller morsels , closer to the street-food roots of the dish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The suya here is heavily seasoned due its marinating , and smoky , too . My suya is two countries mixed , Nigeria and Cameroon . &amp;rdquo ; Best was the toothsome goat suya . ' authentic ' Chinese **28;54824;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Thai Select program assesses cooking methods in restaurant kitchens and verifies their use of Thai ingredients and food products . &amp;ldquo ; At least 60 per cent of dishes offered on the menu must be authentic Thai cuisine and the cooking methods must be the same or very similar to those in Thailand , &amp;rdquo ; says the Thai Select website. &amp;ldquo ; Head chefs may be either Thai or other nationalities . In case of non-Thai head chefs , the chefs must produce proof of at least a two-year experience in cooking Thai foods or possess a Thai cuisine training certificate from an accredited institution . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;54854;TOOLONG ... title= " Par Chiturai , owner of Khao Thai Restaurant in the ByWard Market area . " alt= " Par Chiturai , owner of Khao Thai Restaurant in the ByWard Market area . Khao Thai recently celebrated receiving its " Thai Select " certification of authenticity from the Thai Government , which runs this program for Thai restaurants abroad . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;54890;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1446058 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The program also considers hospitality and atmosphere among its criteria , and Khao Thai certainly qualifies as one of Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s more posh Thai eateries when compared to more humble , mom-and-pop places . Also , according to the Thai Select website , an official from the Thai Trade Office would have visited Khao Thai unannounced and evaluated the dining experience . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Having met the Thai government&amp;rsquo ; s standards , Khao Thai joins about 1,000 other Thai Select eateries around the world , of which 100 are in Canada . Three other Ottawa restaurants &amp;mdash ; Pookie&amp;rsquo ; s Thai on Carling Avenue , Talay Thai in Centretown and Thai Lanna Cuisine in South Keys &amp;mdash ; are similarly designated . So too are Nakhon Thai in Kemptville and Thum&amp;rsquo ; s Kitchen in Cornwall . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; To enjoy Thai dining , you don&amp;rsquo ; t actually need to be in Thailand . The bar is set high and the guidelines are strict , &amp;rdquo ; the website says . &amp;ldquo ; Still , through training and inspections , high standard Thai restaurants worldwide have achieved this distinction . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All that said , Chiturai said her restaurant makes concessions to Canadian palates : &amp;ldquo ; Here we try to keep it authentic , but sometimes Canadians , they can not take the real spice . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;54956;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1446067 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; *** &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For many restaurateurs and restaurant-goers , the notion of authentic cuisine is prized , and even synonymous with quality . If you&amp;rsquo ; ve had it with ketchup-y pad Thai , you know what I mean . If you recoil at Hawaiian pizza and think thin-crust Neapolitan pizza is the one true style by which all pizza should be judged , you concur . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In my reviews of restaurants , I&amp;rsquo ; ve used the word &amp;ldquo ; authentic&amp;rdquo ; scores of times , and always with a positive intention . There are , I think , food traditions worth upholding , which in Canada have often been transported from the Old World to the New World and which speak to the preservation of not only what tastes good , but also of the culture from which the food came . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s something admirable about the Thai Select program , or the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana , which translates to the True Neapolitan Pizza Association and counts among its members more than 800 pizzerias in Italy and beyond , none of which are in Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I would also agree that some inauthentic food could only be considered flops . I&amp;rsquo ; ve had pintxos , the gourmet-level bar snacks of Spain&amp;rsquo ; s Basque region , that were heavenly in their homeland , while crude representations of that kind of cooking in the Ottawa area missed the point utterly . I&amp;rsquo ; d rather skip refrigerated sushi that not only flouts the Japanese standard calling for sushi rice to be warm , at room temperature or even body temperature . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There have also been recent cases in which culinary authenticity , or the apparent lack thereof , became a cause c&amp;eacute ; l&amp;ecirc ; bre , not simply because of ingredients or recipes , but in connection with who was doing the cooking or who owned the restaurant . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In more than a few cases , the same questions kept reverberating . What makes food authentic ? And who gets to decide ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On June , when Shook , a Toronto restaurant that touted itself as serving &amp;ldquo ; modern Israeli cuisine , &amp;rdquo ; opened , some critics on Twitter contended that its fare was Palestinian rather than Israeli , and that the restaurant was guilty of culinary appropriation. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;blockquote class= " twitter-tweet " data-width= " 550 " data-dnt= " true " &gt;&lt;p lang= " en " dir= " ltr " &gt;There 's a new " Israeli " restaurant in Toronto , **27;54986;TOOLONG chef is n't Israeli&lt;br&gt;*No Israelis made up the menu&lt;br&gt;*The name is taken from Arabic&lt;br&gt;*The food is Palestinian &lt;br&gt;*The spices are described as " borrowed " from other **30;55015;TOOLONG is a case of appropriation that must be fought . &lt;a href= " https : //t.co/xO64NtpGru " &gt;pic.twitter ... -- Davide Mastracci ( @DavideMastracci ) &lt;a href= " https : **33;55047;TOOLONG ... 15 , **33;55082;TOOLONG &lt;script async src= " https : **33;55117;TOOLONG " charset= " utf-8 " &gt;&lt;/script&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some responders defended the restaurant , including a writer for Forward.com , a news website for American Jewish readers , who wrote : &amp;ldquo ; No Israelis work in the kitchen at Shook , whose name comes from the Hebrew for &amp;lsquo ; market . &amp;rsquo ; And no Israelis were involved in creating its vegetarian menu , Chef Ben Heaton told the Forward . But a meal there , on a busy recent Wednesday , was all it took to overcome doubts about the cuisine or its authenticity . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When the fast-food restaurant Wolf Down opened in Centretown in May , it raised some eyebrows when it branded its specialty &amp;mdash ; d&amp;ouml ; ner kebab sandwiches &amp;mdash ; as German street food . Wolf Down&amp;rsquo ; s website does acknowledge that Turkish immigrants brought d&amp;ouml ; ner to Germany , but it places greater stress on the &amp;ldquo ; German-ness&amp;rdquo ; of d&amp;ouml ; ner . &amp;nbsp ; While it is true that d&amp;ouml ; ner are immensely popular in Germany , I confess that when an early PR campaign for Wolf Down said &amp;ldquo ; German street food&amp;rdquo ; was on the bill , I awaited sausages with great anticipation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; More problematically , in April , a non-Chinese New York restaurateur opened Lucky Lee&amp;rsquo ; s , with the concept of serving Chinese food that is gluten-free , dairy-free , wheat-free , corn-free , MSG-free and nut-free . Arielle Haspel initially &lt;a href= " https : **33;55152;TOOLONG ... her food as &amp;ldquo ; clean&amp;rdquo ; Chinese cuisine , and she wrote on Instagram : &amp;ldquo ; We heard you&amp;rsquo ; re obsessed with lo mein but rarely eat it . You said it makes you feel bloated and icky the next day ? &amp;rdquo ; After being criticized for cultural appropriation and casting insensitive aspersions at the food she was basing her business on , Haspel took down the Instagram post and apologized at large . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Late last year , Andrew Zimmern , the U.S. food personality , celebrity chef and restaurateur , wound up scalding himself when he &lt;a href= " https : **33;55187;TOOLONG ... his new Chinese restaurant in Minneapolis , Lucky Cricket , and its &amp;ldquo ; authentic&amp;rdquo ; Chinese cooking by saying : &amp;ldquo ; I think I&amp;rsquo ; m saving the souls of all the people from having to dine at these horses&amp;ndash ; t restaurants masquerading as Chinese food that are in the Midwest . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Zimmern subsequently apologized , but not before he endured a slamming from some chefs and pundits . In an opinion piece published in the Washington Post , Ruth Tam wrote that &amp;ldquo ; the Midwest&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;lsquo ; horses&amp;ndash ; t restaurants&amp;rsquo ; are what paved the way for Zimmern&amp;rsquo ; s venture and more broadly , Chinese cuisine in America . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But for all that , I worry that the strictures of culinary authenticity run risks of becoming too limiting . How does a chef &amp;mdash ; or for that matter , a home cook &amp;mdash ; express himself or herself creatively , or satisfy his or her personal palate , beyond simply following the dictates of tradition ? Why can&amp;rsquo ; t fusion food be good ? Why shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t a Chinese chef cook top-notch Japanese food , or a white chef cook traditional Thai fare ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indeed , if culinary authenticity casts back in time and to another place , to how grandma made her perogies or ragu or biryani or curry in the old country , then how do new dishes come to exist ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;55222;TOOLONG ... title= " Koele " Kay " Khutlang , chef and owner of African Grill , poses for a photo at his restaurant in Ottawa Friday Aug 2 , 2019. " alt= " Koele " Kay " Khutlang , chef and owner of African Grill , poses for a photo at his restaurant in Ottawa Friday Aug 2 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;55258;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1446062 " /&gt; **28;55288;TOOLONG MAKES FOOD AUTHENTIC ? **26;55318;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Whether they&amp;rsquo ; re making South African sausages , Northern Vietnamese soups or Neapolitan pizzas , there&amp;rsquo ; s no shortage of Ottawa chefs who proudly and straightforwardly affirm they&amp;rsquo ; re cooking the genuine fare of their homelands . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At African Grill on Clyde Avenue , chef-owner Koele Khutlang cooks suya , the grilled meat of West Africa , and braai , the grilled meat of South Africa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 37-year-old is more closely connected to braai , as he&amp;rsquo ; s from Lesotho , the tiny country encircled by South Africa . The son of a former diplomat at the Lesotho High Commission in Ottawa , Khutlang had planned to work as an electrical engineering technologist and studied at Algonquin College , but more recently he turned to cooking . African Grill , which Khutlang opened in December , is the first restaurant he&amp;rsquo ; s owned by himself . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Khutlang says he&amp;rsquo ; s been perfecting his braai for almost two decades . &amp;ldquo ; For most people who like cooking like me , braai is something you play with , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At African Grill , Khutlang serves chicken and goat braai , with both meats boldly but not overpoweringly spiced , charbroiled and then glazed with a sweet-salty finish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The West African suya that Khutlang offers is another preparation entirely , with bits of heavily spiced and then grilled beef , goat and offal , served with slices of onion and extra chili powder . His recipe is &amp;ldquo ; 90 per cent authentic . &amp;nbsp ; My suya is two countries mixed , Nigeria and Cameroon . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Khutlang says the authenticity of his food stems from spices he imports from Africa . &amp;ldquo ; What I&amp;rsquo ; m targeting is Africans far away from home , to feel at home with the taste of my food , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;55346;TOOLONG ... title= " Peter Tran and his mom Hue Nguyen of the Authentic Vietnamese Pho House with a bowl of their specialty crab soup . August 6 , 2019. " alt= " Peter Tran and his mom Hue Nguyen of the Authentic Vietnamese Pho House with a bowl of their specialty crab soup . August 6 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;55382;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1446059 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Naturally , a restaurant named Authentic Vietnamese Pho House stands up for unadulterated pho and more . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Being 100 per cent real is the best you can get , &amp;rdquo ; says Peter Tran , who with his family owns three Authentic Vietnamese Pho House locations in Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s western suburbs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A cook in a Somerset Street West soup shop for eight years before he opened his first location in 2010 , Tran , 35 , says his soups reflect the tastes of northern Vietnam , where his family is from . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His Bun Rieu crab soup , a specialty little-found in Ottawa , relies on flavours and details that his mother passed on to him , Tran says . His restaurants serve bo luc lac , also known as shaking beef , a Vietnamese specialty that wakes up taste buds with its highly seasoned , savoury dipping sauce . &amp;ldquo ; We do it right , the way they do in Vietnam , &amp;rdquo ; Tran says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That said , Tran makes one allowance for Canadian tastes by offering vegetarian tweaks and options . &amp;ldquo ; In Vietnam , it&amp;rsquo ; s very hard to cook vegetarian food . " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;55448;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1446063 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The owners of Pizza All&amp;rsquo ; Antica , the Manotick Main Street food trailer , say one reason for them selling Neapolitan-style pizzas is that they were tired of driving to Montreal for what they saw as authentic thin-crust pizzas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; ve mastered the recipe of a true Neapolitan pizza , &amp;rdquo ; says Anna Crupi , who co-owns the business &amp;mdash ; its name means Pizza the Antique Way &amp;mdash ; with her husband , Joe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The seasonal business , run by the Barrhaven couple since 2013 , values authenticity so much that Joe looked into securing a membership in the rigorously traditional Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; AVPN regulations call for pizza dough to be made just so , and they state a preference for ingredients to be from Italy&amp;rsquo ; s Campania region , which includes Naples . AVPN-compliant pizza must be stretched by hand so that final diameters do not exceed 35 centimetres . The consistency of the pizza , which must be cooked in a wood-fired oven , should be &amp;ldquo ; soft , easy to manipulate and fold . &amp;rdquo ; The centre should be particularly soft and 0.25 cm in height , plus or minus 10 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At Pizza All&amp;rsquo ; Antica , the pizzas certainly seem like models of authenticity . They are made with sauce and flour sourced from Naples and stretched by the hands of Tina , Anna&amp;rsquo ; s mother , a Naples native . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Joe , who also works as a contractor , took nine days to build his oven and four days to tile the 2,800-pound behemoth , which is mounted in a former landscaping trailer . He went to Boulder , Colorado for a week of intense training in using a wood-fired oven in a mobile environment . Additional pizza-making advice came from Tina&amp;rsquo ; s brother , Franco , a pizzaiolo in Italy for 40 years . Tina would reach out to him on Skype regarding the finer points of pizza . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Joe says he spoke years ago with an AVPN official who was impressed by his business and had never heard of a food truck or trailer that made authentic Neapolitan-style pizzas . One day he might apply for membership , but mostly for the marketing buzz it could confer , he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Besides , for Joe , love , passion and family are the most vital ingredients of the pizzas he sells . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That love , that passion , that bloodline &amp;mdash ; to become more authentic than what we are , it&amp;rsquo ; s almost impossible . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Joe admits to one fact that might ring alarms with the pizza police . " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;55514;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1446064 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; During the past few years in Ottawa , a proliferation of Chinese restaurants opening from downtown to Kanata has driven up the authenticity quotient in Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among them are eateries such as Spicy House on Rideau Street or Delicious Sichuan Cuisine on Prince of Wales Drive , where dishes score much higher in terms of spiciness and pungency compared to the so-called &amp;ldquo ; Szechuan&amp;rdquo ; dishes that first appeared in Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s Chinese restaurants in the 1980s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Other regional Chinese specialties have also arrived . If you didn&amp;rsquo ; t grow up eating potently spicy food , or offal , do you really want to eat what other diners having ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s encouraging that some of the Chinese business owners say authenticity sells not just to expats but to non-Asians who are food-curious or who have already had their tastebuds opened . People have the confidence . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; **28;55704;TOOLONG FUSION FOOD **31;55734;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s kind of a funny trajectory , &amp;rdquo ; says Ottawa chef Tarek Hassan , of his fascination with Cantonese food that goes back more than two decades . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 40-year-old &amp;mdash ; who was born in the Middle East , has spent most of his life in Canada , and who makes Chinese steamed buns to die for at his Gongfu Bao shop on Bank Street &amp;mdash ; offers one of the most thoughtful takes on culinary authenticity I&amp;rsquo ; ve come across . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I distinctly remember the first time I went to a Chinese restaurant , &amp;rdquo ; Hassan continues . &amp;ldquo ; I was in my teens . I was just blown away by the complexity of the flavour and just the whole experience . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hassan moved to Ottawa to attend Carleton University for computer systems engineering , but drifted over to cooking . Roughly a decade ago , he worked at Savana Cafe , the now-closed Centretown restaurant that was an early proponent of multicultural cooking &amp;mdash ; think Thai and Caribbean-influenced dishes on the menu &amp;mdash ; and fusion cooking . &amp;ldquo ; A friend of mine let me know Savana Caf&amp;eacute ; was hiring and it&amp;rsquo ; s a place that had a proper wok station . " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;55803;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1446068 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Seven years ago , when the City of Ottawa put out a call for street food vendors , &amp;ldquo ; steamed buns were a no-brainer , &amp;rdquo ; Hassan says . Years before , he had eaten closed buns from Chinese supermarkets . The game-changing success of New York chef David Chang , who built his Momofuku empire in the 2000s on selling pork belly-filled steamed buns , &amp;ldquo ; inflamed a curiosity , &amp;rdquo ; Hassan adds . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His Gongfu Bao cart debuted in the spring of 2013 near Confederation Park and later won fans at the Westboro Summer Market on Byron Avenue . A year ago , he opened his bricks-and-mortar shop in Centretown. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hassan says he&amp;rsquo ; s faced sceptics who immediately doubted he could make good Chinese food . Selling buns outside Confederation Park , he met a lot of Chinese tourists &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; people who came to Ottawa from China and walked past this cart with this brown guy with a beard serving steamed buns that he&amp;rsquo ; s saying he made , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Their reaction ? &amp;ldquo ; I got anything from , on one extreme , people literally pointing and laughing and continuing to walk , to on the other extreme , people stopping , being curious , asking questions , &amp;rdquo ; Hassan says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve had people specifically say , &amp;lsquo ; You could sell this in China . &amp;rsquo ; Those are the compliments that made my day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t feel entitled to this cuisine , &amp;rdquo ; Hassan continues . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve put a lot of work into developing the craft behind working with it , but I always invite conversations and questions or concerns regarding appropriation because I feel the most important thing is to not be causing any harm . That&amp;rsquo ; s something I take very seriously . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To some degree , for any chef experimenting with food that he or she didn&amp;rsquo ; t grow up with , appropriation may well be baked-in , Hassan suggests . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I recall Jordan Holley , chef de cuisine of Datsun , the modern , pan-Asian restaurant on Elgin Street , addressing his interest in Asian food after I praised his restaurant in a 2015 review : &amp;ldquo ; We respect and appreciate authenticity . But it will always be our interpretation of food , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Holley also offered an anecdote reminiscent of Hassan&amp;rsquo ; s run-ins with Chinese tourists : &amp;ldquo ; We have to admit , we always get nervous when people from strong cultural culinary backgrounds visit Datsun . I think with our culinary training and experience we can feel confident in delivering a flavour that is familiar . For example , we had a friend bring her parents ( old-school Chinese ) , and they were very skeptical to see a young , white , tattooed chef preparing their dinner . They ordered the congee , curry buns , etc. &amp;hellip ; and were extremely impressed . She even told me she never eats congee anywhere other than her mother&amp;rsquo ; s kitchen , not in Hong Kong even , but says ours is an exception . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;55833;TOOLONG ... title= " Tofu bao at Gongfu Bao. " alt= " Tofu bao at Gongfu Bao. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;55869;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1308522 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; For his part , Hassan steeped himself in the tradition of what he&amp;rsquo ; s cooking , using a rolling pin and bamboo baskets to craft and cook his food because after experimenting with more modern measures , he determined that &amp;ldquo ; traditional methods and traditional tools trumped everything . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Furthermore , he continues to delve deep into Cantonese cooking . He visited Hong Kong in 2017 with culinary training in mind , and has &amp;ldquo ; set some thing in motion&amp;rdquo ; for a return trip there . He is looking for a mentor in Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s Chinatown who will help him hone his skills at barbecuing pork &amp;mdash ; a filling for his buns that he prepares even if his parents , for religious reasons , don&amp;rsquo ; t eat pork . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s a little bit of a friction , but I don&amp;rsquo ; t have a problem with it , &amp;rdquo ; Hassan says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hassan feels he can respect authenticity and tradition but also put a personal , Canadian spin on his food . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was letting all the authenticity happen in the buns and the dough , but then I took creative freedom with the fillings , &amp;rdquo ; he says of some experiments during his food-cart days . &amp;ldquo ; For street food , mashups and fusion-y things like that were kind of the norm . People are expecting kind of zany mashup things to happen . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Once , after he ran out of barbecue pork , he made things like bao with halloumi , the brined Cypriot cheese that takes well to grilling . While customers liked the improvised cross-cultural food , Hassan had misgivings . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I realized there&amp;rsquo ; s a big responsibility toward the cuisine I&amp;rsquo ; m working with to , at the very least , represent it in a way that doesn&amp;rsquo ; t confuse people about what it is. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If I&amp;rsquo ; m going to do playful , wacky things , those need to be secondary to me showing someone who&amp;rsquo ; s not familiar with this cuisine what it&amp;rsquo ; s all about . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He calls trendy Asian fusion cooking &amp;ldquo ; dangerous , &amp;rdquo ; explaining that &amp;ldquo ; all these narrative trajectories are going into this melting pot and terminating . And people are losing track of what&amp;rsquo ; s what . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A competent chef might make a reasonable dish from a hodge-podge of Asian ingredients , but it could still be culturally problematic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Here&amp;rsquo ; s some pickled ginger and here&amp;rsquo ; s some gochujang ( a spicy , Korean fermented bean paste ) and here&amp;rsquo ; s some rice , some sesame oil .
