Ottawa 's light rail system comes ungluedhttp : **33;11039;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;11074;TOOLONG ... title= " Public transit in Ottawa : How do we glue it all back together ? " alt= " Public transit in Ottawa : How do we glue it all back together ? " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;11110;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1506691 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among the assorted bugs and gremlins plaguing Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s light-rail system , commuters this week learned of another : a broken weld between two rails . Trains running near Hurdman LRT station had to slow to 10 km/h . To the public , it was a surprising glitch : during a recent six-hour-plus transit commission meeting on rail snafus , staff never raised the possibility of this problem . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet they could hardly have been caught unawares . The builder&amp;rsquo ; s own quality control inspectors , according to the Citizen&amp;rsquo ; s Jon Willing , flagged a defective weld at a maintenance and storage facility during construction . The Rideau Transit Group inspector said instances of failed welds &amp;ldquo ; continue to occur . &amp;rdquo ; In a 2016 report , the inspector also said the ongoing problem was &amp;ldquo ; not acceptable . &amp;rdquo ; The failure may have been caused by storing weld kits in unheated conditions during winter . Hmmm &amp;hellip ; this week&amp;rsquo ; s weld failure came during the first breath of winter weather in Ottawa . Yes , hmmm. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The public will have to wait for the next transit commission meeting for fuller answers on other potential problems , but meanwhile there&amp;rsquo ; s more than enough dismaying news . In barely a week , councillors have gone from bracing for a Transpo price increase to embracing a fare freeze ; from rejecting the return of express bus routes to clamouring for them . Forty buses have been shunted back onto the streets ; the city released route details Friday , even as it scrambles for more vehicles . It needs more drivers too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is happening in a vortex of recriminations and accusations . Aside from blaming RTG for virtually every problem , politicians have verbally attacked citizen transit commissioners ( before apologizing ) ; the mayor delivered a tasteless joke about his own LRT use ( before apologizing ) ; commuters have been injured ( including a broken ankle ) as they slip along wet train or bus platforms ; a female bus driver has been the target of public frustration ; and a&amp;nbsp ; Transpo expert has stopped posting helpful facts about rail due to abuse . The city&amp;rsquo ; s 2020 budgeting plans have &amp;ndash ; if we may use the term &amp;ndash ; gone off the rails . There will be no quick fixes. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;11140;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;11182;TOOLONG ... operators trained to feel bumps that might indicate broken **25;11217;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;11244;TOOLONG ... MacLeod offers provincial help during Ottawa transit **25;11279;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet the city can still do one thing immediately : improve its communications . Crisis experts generally recommend frequent and thorough public updates &amp;ndash ; even when ( especially when ) the news is bad . A daily press briefing , for instance , and frequent feedback meetings for commuters , would help immensely . The mayor should be present for these . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Transit users might be unimpressed at what they&amp;rsquo ; d hear , but at least they&amp;rsquo ; d know what was going on . Lessons from a ' Phoenix suicide ' for the Trudeau governmenthttp : **30;11458;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;11490;TOOLONG ... title= " PSAC members protest the Phoenix pay system on Laurier Avenue last winter . " alt= " PSAC members protest the Phoenix pay system on Laurier Avenue last winter . " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;11526;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1502411 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Almost two years ago , a 52-year-old public servant named Linda Desch&amp;acirc ; telets , suffering from ongoing back pain , battling substance abuse and facing potential financial ruin and the loss of her house , hung herself . There were no signs of forced entry or other violence in her Val-des-Monts home , so coroner Pascale Boulay ruled the death a suicide . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But Boulay also did something unusual : she reviewed Desch&amp;acirc ; telets&amp;rsquo ; work situation at Canada Revenue Agency ; her pay history ; her mortgage obligations and her debt . Boulay concluded that , had the agency been more flexible , Desch&amp;acirc ; telets might still be alive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are lessons here for the next president of the Treasury Board , which deals with the public service . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;11556;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;11598;TOOLONG ... blames Phoenix pay troubles in public servant 's **28;11633;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Desch&amp;acirc ; telets , for example , was approved for special ergonomic equipment at work , but by the time of her death months later , it had not arrived . The rigid rules of the Phoenix pay system also kicked in and pay started to be withheld . Despite her anxious inquiries , and her explanations that her mortgage was in jeopardy , it took direct intervention from her manager to get someone to finally explain she had run out of banked sick days and the system was automatically docking her for time missed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Boulay concluded the woman&amp;rsquo ; s deepening financial crisis was linked to both the Phoenix pay system and to a lack of empathy within the agency . Couldn&amp;rsquo ; t ways have been found to alleviate her immediate financial distress ? Couldn&amp;rsquo ; t the department have advanced her some sick days ? Wasn&amp;rsquo ; t it obvious that a worker&amp;rsquo ; s financial insecurity might cause psychological distress ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In her recommendations , Boulay suggested that the voluntary National Standard of Canada for Psychological Health and Safety in the Workplace be mandatory in the federal public service . She also recommended serious &amp;ldquo ; reflection&amp;rdquo ; on how pay and human resources questions are handled in the bureaucracy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Given the broad distress we know the collapsing Phoenix system has caused , it&amp;rsquo ; s not hard to envisage many other public servants reeling under financial stress as Desch&amp;acirc ; telets did . And it&amp;rsquo ; s odd that the Mental Health Commission&amp;rsquo ; s psychological standard isn&amp;rsquo ; t a stronger part of federal workplace culture . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Prime Minister Justin Trudeau will soon name his cabinet , and the Treasury Board president will be awash in Phoenix problems and systemic morale issues . We&amp;rsquo ; d suggest appointing that minister from among his competent local MPs . Incumbent national capital Liberals have heard for four years about the effects of Phoenix on their constituents , and about the broad challenges of the bureaucracy . Put one in charge &amp;ndash ; and start by handing that person the coroner&amp;rsquo ; s report on Linda Desch&amp;acirc ; telets. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN OPINION&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;11663;TOOLONG ... She was rescued from the train tracks by another commuter and an OC Transpo worker &amp;ndash ; just before a train pulled in. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That near-disaster somehow seems emblematic of all that is amiss with Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s chaotic introduction to light-rail . What else , we are all asking , can go wrong ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For more than a month now , commuters have endured the agony of abruptly delayed or cancelled trains , crowded platforms , Transpo routes that no longer exist , overloaded buses and missed or unreliable connections . Naturally someone would , at some point , fall off a train platform . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , at the commission&amp;rsquo ; s six-hour-plus meeting , senior city and transit staff patiently reviewed LRT&amp;rsquo ; s onboard computer hiccups , jammed doors and malfunctioning track switches . Maintenance-contract payments to the company were now being withheld , with a stern warning that RTG/RTM needed to be ready for winter . It&amp;rsquo ; s far from clear they meant this part . Or that the mayor and city councillors , who are also accountable since they exercise final oversight , are ready to take much blame either . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One can sympathize slightly with the city over this mess . Another 19 will boost the fleet in 2020. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Councillors are quickly finding out this isn&amp;rsquo ; t really a fix , however . By last year , there were 34,862 &amp;ndash ; &amp;shy ; a 78 per cent increase . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Last year , the median wait time for these frail &amp;ndash ; usually elderly &amp;ndash ; people to enter long-term care in this area was 186 days . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Between 2011 and 2018 , the number of long-term care beds in Ontario barely grew , whereas the population 75 years old and up swelled by 20 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; The wait list to get into long-term care will go up over the next five years , despite the Ontario government&amp;rsquo ; s plan to quickly add 15,000 long-term spaces . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you have an elderly relative or friend , you care about this outrageous reality &amp;ndash ; in which frail older couples are sent to different care homes after decades of marriage ; families are given virtually no choice about the quality or location of the long-term home their relative goes to ; people are forced to make long-term care decisions on a few days&amp;rsquo ; notice ; and loved ones deteriorate as they wait months it to access this care . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;12567;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;12609;TOOLONG ... health care will get worse despite massive investment in long-term care , warns fiscal **29;12644;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you don&amp;rsquo ; t have a loved one in this situation , there&amp;rsquo ; s another reason to care : thousands of people who are waiting for long-term care are stuck in hospital beds , a major cause of the &amp;ldquo ; hallway health care&amp;rdquo ; crisis . In late 2018 , 4,600 of Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s 34,000 hospital beds were taken by people waiting for long-term care or rehab. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To its credit , the current Ontario government is frantically adding long-term care spaces , struggling to compensate for the last government&amp;rsquo ; s spending neglect in this area . But as numbers released by the &lt;a href= " https : **33;12675;TOOLONG ... Accountability Officer&lt;/a&gt; show , the fresh spending will merely hold waitlists where they are , not lessen the problem . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Longer-term thinking is imperative . We need real partnerships between retirement homes and long-term care facilities , both in providing care and helping seniors stay healthier for longer so they don&amp;rsquo ; t have to move to long-term care as early . Hiring , training and properly paying personal support workers must also become a priority . And yes , there is room for more private spending by those who can afford it ; government needs to permit this . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The ebb and flow of spending from government to government on long-term beds is no permanent fix &amp;ndash ; as the numbers , and the heartbreaking stories , show . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN CITIZEN OPINIONS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;12710;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;13362;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1488393 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since the 2015 election , Ottawa MPs have been a pretty tame bunch . Even for the few who either made cabinet or became parliamentary secretaries , federal accomplishments on behalf of this city have been relatively modest . Ottawa has been an afterthought to the governing party . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That needs to end ; this IS the nation&amp;rsquo ; s capital , after all . C&amp;rsquo ; mon , re-elected MPs : Time to ensure it&amp;rsquo ; s treated as such . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During the federal campaign , Mayor Jim Watson sent a survey to local candidates laying out what he deems the city&amp;rsquo ; s priorities . These include : a permanent federal fund for public transit ; federal funding for 50 per cent of the cost of LRT Stage 3 ; full federal funding for the Prince of Wales pedestrian-bridge ( though he doesn&amp;rsquo ; t mention the new bridge promised in the 2019 federal budget ) ; doubling gas-tax transfers and indexing them to inflation ; money for affordable housing ; continued financial support to accommodate refugee claimants ; help dealing with guns and gangs ; and federal support for the city&amp;rsquo ; s climate change &amp;ldquo ; adaptation projects . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His list is premised on the hope that the federal level is willing to cough up wads of cash . That&amp;rsquo ; s unlikely , even if the ruling party is not shy about deficit-spending. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s MPs need to get together more . They need an effective urban caucus focused on citywide issues that overlap federal jurisdiction . They need to set priorities and speak with one strong voice . While an individual MP talking about transit money won&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily be heard , six , seven or eight of them speaking in unison will . If this means reaching across party lines through the region &amp;ndash ; gasp ! &amp;ndash ; so be it . Did we elect anybody who does NOT think extending LRT is a good idea ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe src= " **40;13392;TOOLONG ... &lt;p&gt; One priority is clear . Many voters in the Ottawa area worry about climate change ; candidates across all parties told us they heard this consistently at the doors . Local MPs can&amp;rsquo ; t by themselves save the planet , but they can find ways to seriously collaborate &amp;ndash ; with each other and with the city &amp;ndash ; to lessen Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s carbon footprint and aim to make the national capital a model city in the fight to save the environment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To the prime minister-designate himself , here&amp;rsquo ; s another , overdue request : Appoint as the minister responsible for the National Capital Commission an MP who lives here and knows the capital intimately . For four years , the NCC has flagged badly under ministers from Montreal ; it deserves a strong local champion to inject life into its projects and exercise clout at the cabinet table . Start with a focus on LeBreton Flats . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Congratulations on your individual victories , local MPs . You&amp;rsquo ; ve had some practice at this job . " data-portal-copyright= " Sean Kilpatrick " **28;13659;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1486598 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;13689;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; A shout-out to all the local candidates in this federal election . Some have big-party machines behind them ; others are independents with few resources other than their wits . Virtually all are running because they have the best interests of their fellow citizens at heart . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa Centre is one example . It boasts 10 candidates , including a member of the Animal Protection Party of Canada , a Communist , a Libertarian and two independents . The top five parties have all fielded passionate , committed candidates . Public debates have been well attended and mostly polite . It&amp;rsquo ; s like that in other local ridings , too . And , oddly , it leaves one with a sense of optimism about the people who run for office . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Why is this &amp;ldquo ; odd&amp;rdquo ; ? Because at the national level , the campaign has been a desultory , less promising affair . While the parties offer a variety of platform and leadership choices , negativity and character attacks have often overshadowed policy debate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Which brings us back to local candidates . Few people enter politics with the ambition of slagging an opponent or sowing misinformation . Most run because there is a public good they want to achieve , a policy they hope to promote , a vision they have for their community . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;13725;TOOLONG ... OP-EDs&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Ottawa , for instance , that vision might focus on more clean transit , getting shovels in the ground on LeBreton Flats or building another bridge over the Ottawa River . It might include broader goals such as trying to lower taxes generally or increase access to child care . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Once in office , however , a successful local candidate can be engulfed by the pressure to conform , to show unquestioning caucus solidarity , to spout canned statements in Parliament &amp;ndash ; above all to never challenge the leader&amp;rsquo ; s actions . MPs too often fall into the role of photo-op props , all pasted-on smiles and talking points . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;13760;TOOLONG ... full coverage of the 2019 federal election&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Our columnists have written about the difficulty of choosing in this election , and you&amp;rsquo ; ll read more on that between now and Monday . The antidote to this difficulty is taking local candidates seriously and judging them as individuals . Did they show up at all-candidates&amp;rsquo ; meetings ? Have they responded to the questionnaires many groups sent out ? Have they convinced you , in some way , that they are willing to hold government accountable &amp;ndash ; including their own party if it wins &amp;ndash ; by speaking up if they think it is off-track ? Have they convinced you they are independent thinkers ? With incumbents , you can judge their record on this . For challengers , there&amp;rsquo ; s time to do your homework . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Regardless , a shout-out to all for running . This weekend , though , Ottawans may be focused on another topic : the miserable first full week of light rail . And they may well decide whether to risk rail at all on Tuesday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Long delays plagued transit users this past week . On Tuesday , a door broke after a passenger at uOttawa station held it open . Another door jam occurred at Parliament station . On Wednesday , a passenger pried a door open at Lyon station and it stuck . On Thursday , the problem was an onboard computer at Bayview Station . These glitches stopped the system for varying periods . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Explanations have been offered , but there really are no excuses . Problems with the doors were identified during testing of the Confederation Line . That they were not properly fixed , or thoroughly retested prior to service &amp;ndash ; with real people doing what real people do &amp;ndash ; is bewildering . That Transpo technicians were not trained to react quickly ( locking down an affected door so the train itself could get moving again ) is also baffling . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Just as odd was Mayor Jim Watson&amp;rsquo ; s first instinct : to fine or punish people who hold open doors . &amp;ldquo ; There needs to be some punitive measures , &amp;rdquo ; he said . The mayor apparently wants to release video of the incidents in question &amp;ndash ; &amp;ndash ; which is actually a good idea . If the city wants to teach commuters not to hold open train doors , show us what someone did that was so egregious. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , most questions from the Citizen about the manufacture of the doors couldn&amp;rsquo ; t be answered by the city . The train&amp;rsquo ; s builder , Alstom , simply wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t answer them . These were queries such as : &amp;ldquo ; Has this problem occurred in other Alstom trains ? &amp;rdquo ; Watson wants Alstom to explain why our LRT is so &amp;ldquo ; fragile . &amp;rdquo ; He should have asked this months ago . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For the moment , we are left with images of crowds jamming aboard back-up buses , or walking to work this past week ( fortunately , the weather was good ) ; university students , some facing their first exams , scrambling to get to class on time ; and people who struggle with anxiety or claustrophobia trapped amid throngs of surly citizens on overcrowded LRT platforms . The problems of Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s new trains even made national newscasts. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Let&amp;rsquo ; s not call LRT a turkey &amp;ndash ; yet . But Ottawa transit users need a smooth-running week two if they are to stick with their new system . On climate change , do your local election candidates walk the walk ? http : **35;14346;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;14383;TOOLONG ... title= " A large group gathered on Parliament Hill as the Global Climate Protest took to the streets of Ottawa on Friday afternoon . " alt= " A large group gathered on Parliament Hill as the Global Climate Protest took to the streets of Ottawa on Friday afternoon . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;14419;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1473899 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Climate-change rallies were held across Canada Friday in the middle of a federal election campaign , so , naturally candidates from several parties made themselves visible among the participants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But as important as their symbolic presence may have been &amp;ndash ; in Ottawa , Montreal and other cities &amp;ndash ; Canadians should demand much more . They should demand that politicians walk the walk in their personal lives . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To be sure , many parties have set carbon-reduction targets nationally and laid out policies generally that they would pursue if elected . But the effort must be individual too . It&amp;rsquo ; s time for you as a voter to ask wannabe MPs what they&amp;rsquo ; ve done about their own habits to help the environment . That would be a sign of how willing they are to take useful action in office . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For instance ( based on the recommendations many environmental experts have made ) , ask your local candidates about the following : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Have they altered the way they travel from Point A to Point B ? Vehicles are significant contributors to greenhouse gases ; in a single year , driving 10,000 km in a midsize , gasoline-fuelled car emits about 2.2 tonnes of greenhouse gases . Does the candidate own a vehicle ? What kind ? How many ? Has the candidate given up or sold their car ? Switched to an electric vehicle ? Started carpooling ? Do they cycle ? How often do they take public transit , or walk ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;14449;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;14491;TOOLONG ... gather in Ottawa for global climate strike **28;14526;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; How does the candidate heat their dwelling ? Electricity and solar are better than natural gas . A home that has been made energy-efficient helps . Programmable thermostats , not using the cloths dryer as much , unplugging appliances when not in use &amp;ndash ; do your friendly , climate-change-battling neighbourhood candidates do any of these things ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; What are their eating habits ? This isn&amp;rsquo ; t an odd question . The beef industry produces a huge amount of greenhouse gases . According to the World Resources Institute , &amp;ldquo ; If cattle were able to form their own nation , they would rank third behind China and the United States among the world&amp;rsquo ; s largest greenhouse gas emitters . &amp;rdquo ; Cattle need land , water and fertilizers , and they emit a lot of methane . Your local candidates don&amp;rsquo ; t need to be vegans , but if it would be interesting to ask if they&amp;rsquo ; ve cut back animal-based proteins in pursuit of a better planet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; According to the former environmental commissioner of Ontario , a lot of our carbon emissions come simply from having too much stuff . While recycling helps , it doesn&amp;rsquo ; t help a lot . The commissioner&amp;rsquo ; s recommendation : Buy less stuff . How are your local candidates following this advice ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Don&amp;rsquo ; t be afraid to ask federal candidates &amp;ndash ; not just the party leaders &amp;ndash ; any of these questions . Oh , and we should probably ask them of ourselves , too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN OPINION&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;14556;TOOLONG ... letters : Bridges and transit , election thoughts , city planning&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;14591;TOOLONG ... Many Liberals this week made similar statements . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; You would expect such unity from people whose party is under fire . Circle the wagons , defend the boss , deflect , do anything to put the scandal &amp;ndash ; in this case , revelations about Justin Trudeau&amp;rsquo ; s blackface episodes &amp;ndash ; behind you . Toe the party line . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Why is this expected ? Because , fellow voters , we allow it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Citizen argued in this space last week for more onus on the people running locally for federal office . It is their names , not the names &amp;ldquo ; Trudeau , &amp;rdquo ; Scheer&amp;rdquo ; or &amp;ldquo ; Singh&amp;rdquo ; that will appear on your ballot . It follows that anyone , from any party , who hopes to be your MP should be held to a higher standard than merely parroting a script . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; An MP&amp;rsquo ; s job is twofold : a ) represent the riding ; and b ) hold government &amp;ndash ; even if it&amp;rsquo ; s led by one&amp;rsquo ; s own party &amp;ndash ; to account . The blackface controversy is a perfect test of whether local candidates have the gumption to do this . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trudeau&amp;rsquo ; s actions caused deep distress to many Canadians . Others feel that past actions , even foolish ones , don&amp;rsquo ; t define a person&amp;rsquo ; s character . Still others don&amp;rsquo ; t see what the fuss is about . Given such variety of public opinion , what does it say if local candidates are mere echo chambers for party brass in this affair ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So voters : ask local candidates in your riding for their personal take on the past week , not their party line . Ask them for their own &amp;ldquo ; action plans&amp;rdquo ; : If Liberals , what will they do about a leader who acted insensitively in the past ? Will they fight in caucus for concrete measures to heal any rifts caused ? Will they move to sanction the boss for keeping his antics a secret ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ask candidates from opposition parties how they will police their own leaders&amp;rsquo ; behaviour , whether they will reach across parties to try to heal any damage from the blackface saga , what concrete measures , if any , they will take to soften the growing cynicism among voters over this ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Listen carefully to the answers . Is the candidate just repeating what you&amp;rsquo ; re hearing from their leader ? Trying to shift the conversation ? Merely slagging political foes ? Would-be MPs with a backbone will confront this topic frankly &amp;ndash ; perhaps disagree with party bosses , perhaps not . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The week has been a test for Justin Trudeau , but it&amp;rsquo ; s also a test for all candidates . " data-portal-copyright= " Bernard Thibodeau " **28;15040;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1464689 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canadians don&amp;rsquo ; t vote for a prime minister ; they vote for a local member of Parliament . The person you elect in your riding is just as important as the party you support . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yes , yes &amp;ndash ; there is much blathering about how ordinary MPs don&amp;rsquo ; t wield any influence , how they are basically lapdogs for the gang in power , specifically the prime minister . And certainly , Canadians have seen examples of their docility . In the SNC-Lavalin hearings , Liberal committee members burbled canned lines and cut off proper inquiry . Under Stephen Harper , meanwhile , many complained of how the &amp;ldquo ; boys in short pants&amp;rdquo ; routinely ordered backbenchers around . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But there is no rule that says MPs must be trained seals . They&amp;rsquo ; re like that because we don&amp;rsquo ; t demand better . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; You , Ottawa voter , can help change this . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; First , do a little homework . What would YOU identify as the most important issue in your riding that is under federal jurisdiction , and what would you like done about it ? Think seriously about this : If you&amp;rsquo ; re indifferent to your own civic wellbeing , you can hardly blame your MP later for acting with equal passivity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When candidates come to your door , ask bluntly about this important , riding-specific issue and what they plan to do about it &amp;ndash ; even if their own party doesn&amp;rsquo ; t form government , and even if they themselves don&amp;rsquo ; t make cabinet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Next , if the candidate at your door is from the current ruling party , ask him or her not just what the government has accomplished , but what it has done wrong in the past four years . The second question will help you determine if you are dealing with a mouthpiece or an independent thinker. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finally , ask the candidate what he or she will personally do to hold government to account , to exercise oversight on the actions of those in power . The most important role MPs have is to be a check on government action &amp;ndash ; even if their own party governs . Oversight isn&amp;rsquo ; t just for the opposition . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Former Tory MP ( and dissident ) Brent Rathgeber has written : &amp;ldquo ; The test by which we measure a country&amp;rsquo ; s promotion of freedom and democracy is the role , power and efficacy of the elected legislative branch . Is the legislature a meaningful check on executive power or is it purely consultative ? Does the elected assembly actually hold the government to account or is it merely ceremonial ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So don&amp;rsquo ; t just think about which party leader to support . Think about which local candidate ( from any party ) will play their oversight role effectively . " data-portal-copyright= " David Kawai " **28;15689;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1442288 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ontario government says all public schools must have school councils , to keep local school boards accountable and strengthen ties with the community . Increasingly , though , these volunteer bodies have served another crucial purpose : fundraising . And not just for frills or &amp;ldquo ; would be nice&amp;rdquo ; educational extras . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As an investigation by the Citizen&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " https : **33;15719;TOOLONG ... Miller shows&lt;/a&gt; , school councils &amp;ndash ; made up of parents , a community person , a principal , a teacher and sometimes a student &amp;ndash ; often raise thousands to pay for things like iPads , library books and sports equipment . That&amp;rsquo ; s even though the provincially funded public system is supposed to ensure basic educational materials in all public schools . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But as any teacher can tell you , there&amp;rsquo ; s often a gap between what the province provides and what schools need . Given the current government&amp;rsquo ; s desire to control education spending , this gap won&amp;rsquo ; t close soon . So the school councils raise money . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s a hitch , however : the ability of some school councils to raise far more money for their students than others can . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For instance , the school council raised $120,000 in a single year at Rockcliffe Park Public , allowing for new books in the library , a trip to the Ottawa Children&amp;rsquo ; s Festival for all students and a subsidy for the graduation ceremony . By contrast , at Vincent Massey Public , the school council could only raise $4,600 . It simply hopes to upgrade its 1980s-era library books &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The reason for the disparities is clear : the top fundraising school councils tend to be in well-off areas . Parents have more time for volunteer activities such as fundraising , and sometimes possess a wider variety of skills and connections . Those schools where fundraising is much lower often serve poorer neighbourhoods , or have a high ratio of refugee families or recent immigrants . These parents may be working two jobs or still learning English , making it hard to be active members of school councils , let alone handle fundraising . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This results in real education differences within the public board . Given that the province won&amp;rsquo ; t do much anytime soon , the community itself must act . Happily , that is happening in some places . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For instance , some of the top fund-raising councils locally are &amp;ldquo ; twinning&amp;rdquo ; with less well-off ones to ensure they can buy essentials . That&amp;rsquo ; s a great way to help . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The board should also encourage school councils to create a pool of funds among themselves to support all schools . Renfrew 's paramedics show the way for health carehttp : **36;15906;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;15944;TOOLONG ... title= " Renfrew 's paramedics are the only such service in Canada that is allowed to fly drones outside the line of sight . " alt= " Renfrew 's paramedics are the only such service in Canada that is allowed to fly drones outside the line of sight . " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;15980;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1440170 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ontario legislators looking to solve the problem of so-called &amp;ldquo ; hallway medicine&amp;rdquo ; should pay attention to Renfrew County&amp;rsquo ; s community paramedics . After all , health experts from as far away as Australia , the Netherlands and even Turkey are closely studying their work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In an illustration of how locally made decisions can sometimes be better than central ones , the community paramedics have developed unique ways to prevent smaller medical problems from becoming bigger ones . Their work has helped reduce hospital stays and taken pressure off family health care teams . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For example , in addition to handling traditional 911 emergency duties such as stabilizing sick or injured people and getting them to hospital quickly , the Renfrew paramedics also do regular house calls with those who have chronic illnesses &amp;ndash ; checking blood pressure , making sure medicines are taken correctly , finding out if there are new concerns . The mobile medics see more than 1,500 clients at home on a routine basis . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And because their geographic coverage area is the largest of any service in Ontario ( it sprawls from the fringes of Ottawa up to Algonquin Park ) , these paramedics also monitor patients remotely through an electronic health record system they developed with a Quebec tech company . Their system is now used by several other services in Eastern Ontario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Other technology is also used : Drones , for instance , can bring portable defibrillators and various medical supplies to remote areas of the county even before the ambulance arrives . As Citizen reporter Elizabeth Payne &lt;a href= " https : **33;16010;TOOLONG ... in a recent feature&lt;/a&gt; , Renfrew is the only paramedic service in Canada that is allowed to use drones beyond line-of-sight. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Clearly , the Renfrew paramedics have a great deal to teach other emergency services &amp;ndash ; which is why the Ontario government needs to learn from them . The province currently plans to blend 52 municipal paramedic services across Ontario into 10 regional ones . By doing so , it hopes to improve co-ordination and front-line care . The amalgamation plan fits into a wider project to centralize more health care decisions as the government tackles a shortage of hospital and long-term care beds. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But centralization , tempting as it is , doesn&amp;rsquo ; t always provide the best answers . Sometimes innovation comes from letting local health care experts identify and solve problems . Renfrew&amp;rsquo ; s paramedic model has shown how creative solutions can be found by caring people who know their communities better than a well-meaning bureaucracy in a larger regional centre ever will . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Let&amp;rsquo ; s hope the health minister spends time in Renfrew carefully observing &amp;ndash ; and learning &amp;ndash ; as the paramedics continue their inventive approaches to saving lives . &lt;/p&gt; Ottawa Citizen Editorial BoardSat , 03 Aug 2019 11:00:32 **45;16045;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;16518;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1425323 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A &amp;ldquo ; giant radiator . &amp;rdquo ; &amp;nbsp ; A &amp;ldquo ; shipping container . &amp;rdquo ; &amp;nbsp ; An &amp;ldquo ; imminent act of vandalism . &amp;rdquo ; These phrases have all been directed at the proposed addition to the Ch&amp;acirc ; teau Laurier . On Wednesday , Ottawa Council will be asked to rescind its approval of the capital&amp;rsquo ; s least popular architectural project in decades . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Conflicting ambitions , tone deafness and craven politics led to this mess . Let&amp;rsquo ; s identify some key lessons . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;For city council : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It should be clear by now that abdicating decisions to staff on issues of deep citywide interest &amp;ndash ; particularly those that touch people emotionally &amp;ndash ; is plain bad leadership . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In June 2018 , the city&amp;rsquo ; s built heritage subcommittee , which was then chaired by Tobi Nussbaum , recommended conditional approval of a much-criticized version of the ch&amp;acirc ; teau addition that was before it at the time . The motion , seconded by unelected vice-chair Barry Padolsky , included several changes to satisfy the conditions . It also recommended that city staff assess whether hotel owner Larco Investments had met these criteria , and made clear that final approval would rest with planning staff . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Full council eagerly signed off on this approach . After all , directing staff to shoulder the key decision was an ingenious way to douse a potential political firestorm right before a municipal election campaign was to start . But it wasn&amp;rsquo ; t responsible politics . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; City staff have approved the latest version of the design . Now council faces a public that can&amp;rsquo ; t understand why elected officials are unable to overturn approvals without placing taxpayers at high risk of huge legal costs . In future , council , don&amp;rsquo ; t shovel aside big decisions . It&amp;rsquo ; s not why we elected you . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;For Larco Investments : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Larco&amp;rsquo ; s exasperation is understandable : It is now on its fifth iteration of the addition , is bearing all costs associated with expanding the hotel , and has followed all the rules . Owning a high-profile , skyline-defining building steeped in history and romance demands an approach that is more than legalistic . Larco feels its design is respectful of the ch&amp;acirc ; teau&amp;rsquo ; s lineage , but it has not done a good job of explaining why . Modern architecture is not the fort&amp;eacute ; of most people . But Ottawans can accept ( and even love ) a good deal of &amp;ldquo ; modern&amp;rdquo ; architecture if they understand it . " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;17012;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1423467 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; No one enjoys being left on hold when trying to access a customer service . That&amp;rsquo ; s why modern-day companies and governments allow us to make reservations or fill out forms or submit applications online . It&amp;rsquo ; s efficient and effective . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But not if you&amp;rsquo ; re Para Transpo , the city&amp;rsquo ; s public transportation system for people whose disabilities prevent them from using OC Transpo . To arrange a ride with Para Transpo , clients must telephone in advance and reserve . This captive audience reports frequent , impossibly long waits to reach a representative by telephone &amp;ndash ; as long as two hours . Para Transpo considers it reasonable if a caller waits 15 to 20 minutes to connect with someone to make a booking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is outrageous in a capital city . Ottawa Council should be ashamed . Instead , it waffles on helping disadvantaged citizens travel a bit more easily to medical appointments , shopping activities or jobs . The very people who need the city&amp;rsquo ; s help the most are tethered to their telephones , their lives quite literally on hold . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; New city councillor Rawlson King recently asked about introducing an online reservation system for Para Transpo . Toronto has had a system for a decade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; City staff recommended online booking back in 2013 . But the Transit Commission deferred further action , holding public consultations in 2015 and again in 2018 . Staff reported that not all customers were sure they&amp;rsquo ; d like online booking . Fair enough ; not everyone has easy access to the Internet. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But that&amp;rsquo ; s not the whole context . What Para Transpo customers want &amp;ndash ; what everyone wants when they use any service &amp;ndash ; is a system that is fair , efficient and accessible for them . Para Transpo could offer both an online portal and a properly staffed telephone service so that Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s most vulnerable could use either method and not constantly be treated as a transit afterthought . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The city itself admits they&amp;rsquo ; re not a priority . In a written response to King , the director general of the transportation services department says , &amp;ldquo ; At this time , staff are primarily focussed ( sic ) on the opening of O-Train Line 1 , the Confederation Line , which will benefit all customers . &amp;rdquo ; No , it&amp;rsquo ; ll benefit people who are physically and mentally able to use it . The others , the ones who have no choice but to suffer interminable delays for Para Transpo , will have to await a staff report &amp;ldquo ; later this year . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Transit lobby groups often urge councillors to ride OC Transpo so they can understand its problems . If they don&amp;rsquo ; t , more malign players will fill the space . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet governments blithely ignore this responsibility . Since its mandate isn&amp;rsquo ; t enshrined in legislation , it&amp;rsquo ; s impossible to know if the centre will be a good or bad thing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , back to that vacuum . " data-portal-copyright= " Sean Kilpatrick " **28;18289;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1389390 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The military , city staff and a muscular army of volunteers have delivered more than 1.5 million sandbags during the 2019 flooding season , in a determined bid to save homes and businesses . But as effective as sandbags can be , filling them is also a back-wrenching process , as anyone who has spent a few hours shovelling or lifting knows . Is there a better way ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Citizen reporter Joanne Laucius recently found that more sophisticated &amp;ndash ; and effective &amp;ndash ; techniques for holding back the waters do indeed exist . With more extreme weather expected in future , all levels of government should jointly explore these technologies . Particularly since some are Canadian innovations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the moment , city officials won&amp;rsquo ; t say what they think about alternatives to sandbagging . Still engulfed in the crisis that has hit so many residents , their horizon is short . They promise a full review of the flood response . That review should include a thorough examination of at least three Canadian-made products : the Water-Gate , made in Victoriaville , Que. , and two products sold by Calgary&amp;rsquo ; s Tiger Dam Systems . Other products also deserve a look , and Laucius describes them &lt;a href= " https : **33;18319;TOOLONG ... . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some devices use the water itself to create and anchor synthetic dams that are easier and quicker to deploy than sandbags ( sometimes more expensive , too ) , and can be reused . Others are simply engineered as strong , stable barriers . &amp;nbsp ; A U.S. military facility is used for testing , and in many cases such products have &amp;ldquo ; significantly outperformed&amp;rdquo ; sandbags , says one scientist with the Coast and Hydraulics Laboratory said . The three Canadian products named above were certified by that lab . Unfortunately , Canada doesn&amp;rsquo ; t do its own testing . It should . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;18354;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;18396;TOOLONG ... is slow work that requires hundreds of helpers . When our political leaders , experts and the public sit down for what one hopes will be transparent , open sessions to assess the lessons of 2017 and 2019 , they must start with flood avoidance , not mitigation . A better understanding of floodplains , shared with all concerned parties ; better regulation of where human structures can be built ; incentives to move from vulnerable zones to safer ones ; more robust wetlands protection ; and a clear understanding of what is going on all the way up the Ottawa River as well as in the major urban centres &amp;ndash ; all of these things must be addressed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then , governments should delve into the best technologies to protect property . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;18756;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1395316 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shredding and sorting paper may not sound to some people like an ideal career . But to 34 developmentally disabled Ottawa adults , it has been a positive , essential experience . So let&amp;rsquo ; s find a way to save their jobs &amp;ndash ; or offer them a plan that is equally constructive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The background : For almost four decades , the federal government has employed developmentally challenged adults in this structured work , originally for Library and Archives Canada but now for a variety of departments . The program is run by the Ottawa-Carleton Association for Persons with Developmental Disabilities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s value to processing all that federal paper waste , but the real bonanza is how it teaches the workers important basic skills : showing up reliably and punctually ; completing a task ; practising social interaction . In the private sector , it&amp;rsquo ; s hard to find the right blend of job opportunities for a first-time worker who struggles with challenges . Yet many of these workers have eventually been able to move successfully to other employment . There are currently 34 people in the program . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The program is now threatened mostly for money reasons : Until recently , the workers were paid an honorarium of $2,000 annually . New rules say they must be compensated at minimum wage , $14 an hour for the hours they work . The Liberal government have extended the program a year but says it will end in 2020. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Understandably , both the workers and their families are upset . Conservative leader Andrew Scheer called it a &amp;ldquo ; costly and heartless&amp;rdquo ; decision . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Admittedly , this is not a simple issue . Some argue that the actual tasks being performed by these employees are diminishing in importance as the market for recycled paper products shrinks . Others decry segregated workforces as &amp;ldquo ; tokenism. &amp;rdquo ; It may be that there are other , more practical means of supporting this cohort . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But saving money by ending the program is an illusory goal . One family wrote to us that when their son was receiving only the honorarium , he could claim a provincial disability pension as well . Now that he is at minimum wage , the provincial pension is reduced accordingly . In other words , governments pay , one way or another . being paid to perform a task is always better . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Liberal Minister of Public Services Carla Qualtrough has made positive , if vague , statements about being committed to new jobs for the workers , and we don&amp;rsquo ; t doubt her sincerity . But words won&amp;rsquo ; t make it so . Ms. Qualtrough , show us a specific , compassionate and useful plan to employ these people who are so eager to work . &lt;/p&gt; Ottawa Citizen Editorial BoardSat , 11 May 2019 11:00:41 **45;18786;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;18908;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1390319 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Amid forecasts of actual sunlight this weekend , there was a sense by Friday that Ottawa might have seen the worst of the flooding , that things might settle down in the coming weeks , that the time was approaching for stock-taking and longer-term thinking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So let&amp;rsquo ; s stand back and review the past few weeks : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Although the flooding has devastated many homes in Ottawa , Gatineau and the Valley , thousands of people pitched in to help out . Spontaneous displays of altruism , apparent last fall when the tornadoes hit , resurfaced . Strangers filled sandbags , neighbours housed neighbours , cash and food donations abounded . High school groups , the intrepid West Carleton Warriors , the Ottawa 67&amp;rsquo ; s and so many other groups and individuals unhesitatingly lent a hand . Ottawa is a generous city . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Given some warning of what was coming , the mayor rightly declared a state of emergency early , bringing in the armed forces to fill sandbags , shore up berms and co-ordinate much of the manpower needed to hold back the raging river . Wisely , officials closed the vulnerable Chaudi&amp;egrave ; re bridge for the duration . The city arranged regular daily briefings to share information as quickly as possible , and used social media effectively . Unexpected side issues such as the sewer backup in Westboro&amp;nbsp ; caused inconvenience but were handled as reasonably as possible in the short term . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; There were inevitable miscues , such as an over-broad decision to shut down electricity to some homes that had a fighting chance of holding back the waters . Still Hydro One appeared to recognize this and was attempting to assess individual circumstance as the week went on . Lesson learned , perhaps . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;18938;TOOLONG ... title= " A little hope flowers in an inundated Ottawa neighbourhood as Canadian Armed Forces flood relief operations continue . " alt= " A little hope flowers in an inundated Ottawa neighbourhood as Canadian Armed Forces flood relief operations continue . " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;18974;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1391383 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet as complex as the flood response was , longer-term planning will be trickier : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; The city &amp;ndash ; and developers &amp;ndash ; need updated mapping and a fuller understanding of floodplains . Once the city has this data in hand , council must act rationally : Approving development in highly vulnerable areas needs a sober rethink . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Ottawa , the province and federal government must craft an incentive strategy to dissuade people from building in flood-prone areas , or provide one-time support to help them relocate . This strategy might follow the Quebec model of hard caps on flood compensation , for instance , or borrow from policies used in other countries . The United Kingdom has a special insurance program , while the Dutch have allowed more room around rivers to accommodate natural change . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Whatever our policy looks like , financially assisting property owners to build , rebuild or renovate in flood zones would be short-sighted . As generous as Ottawans are , prevention is better than triage. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;19004;TOOLONG ... " alt= " Light Rail Train ( LRT ) at the Blair Station on March 20. " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;19230;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1386431 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; When an enterprise is as ambitious as Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s light-rail project , there are bound to be a few problems . But a year after the Rideau Transit Group was initially supposed to turn over to the city a passenger-ready service , the glitches have grown more worrisome. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The latest development is the departure , announced Thursday , of Chris Swail , the city&amp;rsquo ; s senior planning official for Stage 2 of the LRT . Swail&amp;rsquo ; s leave-taking , reportedly to spend more time with his family , feels abrupt : His last day at work was Friday . According to official explanations , since the contracts have been approved and no more city &amp;ldquo ; planning&amp;rdquo ; is needed on Stage 2 , Swail has no further work to do on the file . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fine . But , added to other recent , confidence-shrivelling events , this HR bulletin doesn&amp;rsquo ; t exactly suggest that Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s city government is #Ready4Rail. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here&amp;rsquo ; s a quick overview of a few project headaches that came to light in 2019 : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; The Rideau Transit Group said it would miss its March 31 deadline to hand over a completed Stage 1 LRT to the city . The project has now missed three deadlines and no official new target date has been set for the city takeover . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; The estimated cost of Stage 2 has been readjusted upward by $1.2 billion , rising from $3.4 billion to about $4.66 billion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Inspection reports obtained by the Citizen suggest shoddy work inside the Confederation Line tunnel will probably mean ongoing water leakage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;bull ; Based on internal documents , the CBC reported that the Stage 1 LRT trains might not be tough enough to tackle Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s winters . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then , of course , there was the Stage 2 procurement mess , in which the CBC revealed that while SNC-Lavalin had won the bid for the $1.6-billion Trillium Line , it had not met the minimum technical score required for consideration . City staff said they couldn&amp;rsquo ; t answer questions about this , but council approved it anyway , settling for a future study by the city&amp;rsquo ; s auditor general of the Stage 2 procurement process . SNC , you&amp;rsquo ; ll remember , is also the firm that&amp;rsquo ; s wrapped up in that pesky Jody Wilson-Raybould affair federally. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And oh yes , Stage 2 has been pushed back two years from its initial schedule . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , the same city government that has just declared a state of emergency over floods , and also declared a very-much-related climate change emergency , faces ongoing challenges with the most important element of its greenhouse-gas reduction strategy : the launch of a successful light-rail system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Is Ottawa #Ready4Rail ? Lessons from an Ottawa woman 's suicidehttp : **33;19307;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;19342;TOOLONG ... title= " Lauren Richards with dog , Buster . Richards took her own life on Feb. 21 , 2019. " alt= " Lauren Richards with dog , Buster . Richards took her own life on Feb. 21 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;19378;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1383545 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indescribable mental agony . Deep depression . Emotional chaos . The inescapable terror that one&amp;rsquo ; s life is being torn apart . It&amp;rsquo ; s a constant reality for many Canadians struggling with suicidal thoughts . In today&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " https : **33;19408;TOOLONG ... , Citizen writer Joanne Laucius tells the story of one young woman who ultimately lost her battle to survive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lauren Richards was a friendly , talented 26-year-old when she took her life , barely two months ago . She had struggled since her teen years , and was diagnosed with both depression and possible borderline personality disorder . Her parents and friends decided to share details of her journey in hope of finding answers , and helping others . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Those answers will not be easy to discover , but we know they must be pursued . About 11 people in Canada die from suicide each day , and , as Laucius reports , it is the second leading cause of death ( after accidents ) for those aged 15-34. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lauren Richards&amp;rsquo ; difficult , searingly painful experience suggests at least some areas for improvement . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; First , it is clear from her experience that the stigma surrounding mental illness is far from over . Bell Let&amp;rsquo ; s Talk campaigns and other concrete steps to help society understand and accept that mental illness is just that &amp;ndash ; an illness , not a choice or moral failing &amp;ndash ; have accomplished much , but not enough . Richards , and others like her , often go to great lengths to hide their anguish or self-harm . Just weeks before her death , she posted on Instagram : &amp;ldquo ; Going to lose my mind , not because I have BPD , but because of all the stigma attached to it . PLEASE educate yourself before you judge me. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Second , although a parade of compassionate mental health care providers worked with her , Richards , like so many others , confronted &amp;ldquo ; revolving-door syndrome&amp;rdquo ; throughout her years of treatment , such as changes in doctors and mental health workers . With each new face , says one friend , &amp;ldquo ; She had to re-tell her story every time . &amp;rdquo ; She was terrified when a psychotherapy program that seemed to be helping her came to an end . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;19443;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;19485;TOOLONG ... Richards took her own life at 26 . She left behind devastated loved ones and a haunting **29;19520;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;19551;TOOLONG ... policies in Canada and beyond : What 's working and what needs to **27;19586;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Third , the families of those struggling with fragile mental health also need more support . Richards&amp;rsquo ; loving family did everything possible to support her , but her mother notes that dealing with her daughter was often overwhelming . Health professionals need to educate and support families too , says Jennifer Richards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Suicidal people are some of the most vulnerable among us . Yet mental health pain continues to be viewed differently from physical ailments . Perhaps the Richard family&amp;rsquo ; s brave sharing of Lauren&amp;rsquo ; s story will help change that . Something must . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;19615;TOOLONG ... Ontario 's long road to balanced budgetshttp : **33;19767;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;19802;TOOLONG ... title= " Ontario Finance Minister Vic Fedeli presents the 2019 budget in the legislature Thursday . " alt= " Ontario Finance Minister Vic Fedeli presents the 2019 budget in the legislature Thursday . " data-portal-copyright= " Frank Gunn " **28;19838;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1380094 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yes , there are the inevitable shots at the former Kathleen Wynne government . For instance , &amp;ldquo ; This is a budget &amp;hellip ; that , after years of neglect , puts the people first . &amp;rdquo ; And yes , there are reminders of how people were &amp;ldquo ; overtaxed and over-regulated&amp;rdquo ; under the provincial Liberals . But mostly , Ontario Finance Minister Vic Fedeli&amp;rsquo ; s 2019 budget focuses on easing fears that the Progressive Conservatives want to slash spending no matter the consequences . Turns out , they don&amp;rsquo ; t. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mind you , this more &amp;ldquo ; balanced approach&amp;rdquo ; leaves the PCs playing the same game governments of all stripes tend to indulge in : stretching out the path back to balanced budgets over several years &amp;ndash ; into the next term , in fact , in 2023-24 . It will also take until 2022-23 to get the province&amp;rsquo ; s net debt-to-GDP ratio under 40 per cent . This from the party that , during the 2018 election campaign , seemed to think it would be easy to find flab . Instead , the Tories , having directed their ministries to identify administrative savings of four per cent , still need extra time to get the province out of the red . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;19868;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;19910;TOOLONG ... Ford delivers a politically , if not fiscally , balanced **27;19946;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;19975;TOOLONG ... await funding details ; planning for new Civic , treatment centre get budget **25;20010;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;20037;TOOLONG ... Ottawa officials breathe sigh of relief at provincial **27;20072;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Give them credit , though : They are trying to move spending in the right direction , and not to inflict too much pain along the way ( If you do think the cuts are too deep , well , they&amp;rsquo ; re making it easier to ease your anxiety over a drink ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In fact , there is modest help in some areas . The government proposes , for instance , a new tax credit for families , letting them decide how to spend their money . It will start helping low-income seniors with dental care . And while the PCs are seen as business-friendly , they held off this year on the corporate tax cut promised in the election . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For Ottawa , there is already-announced money for Stage 2 LRT , some funding to push along the new Civic Hospital campus , and a tip of the fiscal hat for policing . Perhaps most importantly , given his earlier concerns , Mayor Jim Watson hasn&amp;rsquo ; t identified any downloading of provincial responsibilities onto the city . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That doesn&amp;rsquo ; t mean everyone will be happy . While health care spending will rise , it won&amp;rsquo ; t be by much . Post-secondary education loses money , and the majority of university and college funding will be tied to performance . These institutions are already feeling the impact . The environment clearly won&amp;rsquo ; t be a priority for the government , which is fighting the federal carbon tax . And Indigenous services also face belt-tightening. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some of this may hurt over the long run . But the government believes , as we do , that steaming further toward the debt abyss will hurt much more . Fedeli wants a slow , steady fiscal turn . " data-portal-copyright= " Justin Tang " **28;20326;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1375872 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In her unsuccessful written plea to remain a member of the federal Liberal caucus , Jody Wilson-Raybould wrote to her fellow MPs : &amp;ldquo ; Ultimately the choice that is before you is about what kind of party you want to be a part of , what values it will uphold , the vision that animates it , and indeed the type of people it will attract . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Well , we now know &amp;ndash ; with dismaying clarity &amp;ndash ; which sort of values , vision and people &amp;ldquo ; animate&amp;rdquo ; the Liberal party , or at least which are preferred by its elected members . And this revelation is , to use the vocabulary of Jane Philpott , the other MP ejected from caucus , &amp;ldquo ; disheartening. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;20356;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;20398;TOOLONG ... of women turn their backs on Trudeau in the House as he addresses Daughters of the **25;20433;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;20460;TOOLONG ... ejects Wilson-Raybould , Philpott from Liberal **27;20495;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;20524;TOOLONG ... Expulsions accomplish nothing but vindictiveness for vindictiveness 's **25;20559;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;20586;TOOLONG ... is pushing you out ' : Texts between Butts and Wilson-Raybould show mounting anger , frustration over **28;20621;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;20651;TOOLONG ... the statement Jane Philpott issued after Justin Trudeau expelled her from the Liberal Party **27;20686;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;20715;TOOLONG ... Trudeau Liberals revealed their true selves to Canadians long ago&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; In rejecting an honest , complete discussion of the facts around the SNC-Lavalin mess , then exiling two respected , once-senior cabinet ministers over their defence of prosecutorial independence , Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and his caucus have shown that political expediency trumps principle , loyalty trumps independent thought , and prevarication trumps transparency . As with any tinpot government , ends justify means , the leader is supreme , and thoughtful reflection belongs &amp;ndash ; well , anywhere but among elected members . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Does this seem harsh ? Then let&amp;rsquo ; s review the basics : Former attorney general Wilson-Raybould , who had been shuffled out of the job , revealed during committee testimony that for months she had felt inappropriate political pressure to overrule the decision of an independent prosecutor who wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t cut a remediation deal with SNC-Lavalin on charges of corruption and bribery . Painstakingly , Wilson-Raybould documented what had led her to deem the pressure inappropriate . Officials who attempted to rebut her were broadly unable to do so . Perhaps there were better counter-arguments to be had , or facts the public does not yet understand , but the Liberal-majority committee refused to hear them . Meanwhile , the government&amp;rsquo ; s version of the saga evolved from vague denial to the message that if it indeed had tried to interfere with an independent prosecution , well , there were jobs at stake . Ends justify means . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Next came a cynical barrage of character assassination and insinuation , leaks about judges , and faux outrage at Wilson-Raybould for offering up a ( legal ) tape of a phone call . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20750;TOOLONG ... title= " In this file photo taken on Feb. 27 , former Justice Minister and Attorney General Jody Wilson-Raybould arrives to give her testimony about the SNC-Lavalin affair before a justice committee hearing on Parliament Hill . " alt= " In this file photo taken on Feb. 27 , former Justice Minister and Attorney General Jody Wilson-Raybould arrives to give her testimony about the SNC-Lavalin affair before a justice committee hearing on Parliament Hill . " data-portal-copyright= " LARS HAGBERG " **28;20786;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1375881 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It all leads to the conclusion that the Liberal caucus , and its leader , have rejected the first role of MPs : to hold government to account . Under our system of responsible government , elected houses supposedly control the executive branch , not the other way around . Governments are supposed to answer to democratically elected members . The principle applies not merely to the opposition but to governing party MPs . They are not supposed to be puppets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This seemingly straightforward job requirement has been trampled over the decades , of course . Government MPs on committees are often mere mouthpieces for the boss . Backbench queries during Question Period are regularly cheerleader sessions for the PM . It&amp;rsquo ; s not that the Liberal party under Trudeau is any worse than predecessor governments , including Conservative ones ; it&amp;rsquo ; s simply that these are the Liberals who , in 2015 , promised to take the taint and cynicism out of politics . Apparently only two Grit MPs took this pledge seriously . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alongside hypocrisy and cowardice , the Liberals&amp;rsquo ; current position oozes irony . For example , having spent three years releasing members of the Senate from the shackles of party discipline , on the premise that this would strengthen thoughtful debate in the red chamber , Trudeau is clearly having none of it with his elected caucus . Only two felt that truth , accountability and transparency were essential parts of their job . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The party has indeed chosen how it wants to operate . Shame . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN OPINIONS : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;20816;TOOLONG ... Better bridges but a muddled approach to affordable housinghttp : **33;20968;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;21003;TOOLONG ... title= " New housing construction . " alt= " New housing construction . " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;21039;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1326580 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa , like many cities , faces two major challenges : transportation infrastructure and affordable housing . Tuesday&amp;rsquo ; s federal budget &amp;mdash ; the last before October&amp;rsquo ; s election &amp;mdash ; contains good news on the first , much more mixed news on the second . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Commuters in Ottawa and West Quebec will be happy that the government plans to replace the 100-year-old Alexandra Bridge , refresh its studies of Ottawa River crossings and provide millions of dollars to upgrade existing bridges . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , if you&amp;rsquo ; re an aspiring homeowner with a family income of less than $120,000 , the budget offers , via the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp. , a boost to your down payment . You likely won&amp;rsquo ; t have to repay it until you sell the house , perhaps decades from now . While the details weren&amp;rsquo ; t available Tuesday , it looks like an interest-free , long-term loan from the government . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is seductive but wrong-headed . No one denies there are housing &amp;mdash ; especially affordable housing &amp;mdash ; shortages . In Ottawa , for instance , the rental vacancy rate was a miserly 1.7 per cent in 2017 . The federal government is apparently so worried about the city that it is giving Claridge Homes $70.8 million for a 27-storey building in which more than 200 units will be lower-rental. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now the Liberals offer what&amp;rsquo ; s called the First-Time Home Buyer Incentive , under which qualifying buyers get a 10-per-cent shared-equity mortgage for a newly constructed home , or five per cent for an existing home , thanks to a $1.25-billion fund ( over three years ) from CMHC . The deal means buyers can save on their monthly payments , &amp;ldquo ; giving them more money to pay down their insured mortgage sooner or for other priorities . &amp;rdquo ; This will be available before the election . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Why , though , should Canadians get interest-free loans on the backs of other taxpayers to buy a house ? And why is the government introducing a plan that seems to fly in the face of its own &amp;ldquo ; stress test&amp;rdquo ; principles , meant to ensure homebuyers don&amp;rsquo ; t overextend in the first place ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are further workarounds in the budget , like raising the amount you can take tax-free from your Registered Retirement Savings Plan to purchase or build a home . Such incentives risk unintended consequences : If enough people take up these offers , they might drive up the demand , and thus the price , for housing &amp;mdash ; which undermines the initial intent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you think the government knows what it&amp;rsquo ; s doing , consider : It will also provide $300 million for a new Housing Supply Challenge so stakeholders can pitch ideas to &amp;ldquo ; break down the barriers that limit the creation of new housing . &amp;rdquo ; And there&amp;rsquo ; s the recently announced expert panel , focused on British Columbia , to look at future housing affordability. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One might think a government interested in helping lower-income people to afford decent housing would simply hand them a direct subsidy , and let them choose how to spend it : renting , saving for a house , whatever their most pressing shelter priority was . One might think that same government would encourage cities to consider more flexible zoning rules , or chat with provinces about loosening rent controls , so that the market itself had more flexibility to offer a variety of housing types . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But no , that would not be in the spirit of fiddling that governments tend to prefer . And it wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t hand anyone a cash advance before voting day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , let&amp;rsquo ; s at least praise the building of bridges . The building of affordable housing , however , is a more muddled matter . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; MORE BUDGET COVERAGE : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21069;TOOLONG ... budget 2019 : Ottawa-Gatineau bridge battle revived as budget renews controversial project&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21104;TOOLONG ... housing and infrastructure : What Ottawans need to know about this year 's federal budget&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21139;TOOLONG ... budget 2019 : Bagnall : Phoenix Pay 's cumulative cost overruns soon to top $800 million&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21174;TOOLONG ...
